AdminTracker.text:
# Viper OS Admin & In-app Tracker

> **Status:** implemented in GDScript and headless-tested with Godot 4.7.2 (`tests/admin_tests.gd`: 92 checks). Everything is **local only**: no accounts, no servers, no network. Built on Foxy's Phoenix Glass kit (PR #17); see [UI_DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md](UI_DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md) §8.

Open it from the radial launcher (**12 o'clock ◎ Admin**) or MENU › 🛡 Viper Admin (`UIRoot.open_admin()`). Security (lock, PIN, e-stop, audit, backup) is at **2 o'clock 🛡** on the radial. All routes are in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md#access-paths-where-to-find-each-screen).

## Screens (portrait 720×1280, five swipeable tabs)
| Tab | What it shows | Kit pieces used (§8) |
|---|---|---|
| Home | Ticket rings (open / accepted / closed), pending brain proposals, companion energy (fire rings), revisions per day (LineGraph + hero `rN`), text report | GlassCard, RingStat, LineGraph |
| Tickets | Segmented filters (Open/New/Mine/Closed/All). Admin-table pill rows (avatar ring, `#id summary`, one status chip). **Swipe left** on a row for workflow actions. Tap a row to open a detail card with comments and links. 7 rows, then pages. | SegmentedPills, PillRow, PagedList, Toast |
| Wiki | Pages / Recent filter, pill rows, rendered page with Trac-style links, Edit → Save (new revision), History | same + RichTextLabel links |
| Timeline | Ring timeline, one day at a time (‹ › or swipe). Git commits + in-app revisions. Tap to expand into a glass card with the diff. **Hold 0.6 s to revert.** | RingTimeline, HoldButton |
| Profile | Sign-up stepper: name → avatar → voice → realm → done. Ring progress, 64 px inputs, primary pill at the bottom, swipe right to go back, phoenix burst at the end. After that, a profile card. | SignupStepper, RingStat |

New kit components (in `scripts/ui/kit/`, built to the §8 specs): `SwipePages`, `SegmentedPills`, `PillRow`, `PagedList`, `RingTimeline`, `Toast`, `HoldButton`, `SignupStepper`. `scripts/admin/ui/viper_kit.gd` is a thin helper over `themes/phoenix_glass.tres`, `PhoenixTokens` and `scenes/ui/kit/*`. It defines no colors of its own.

Not in this PR: §9 (3D companion nameplates and auras) and §10 (minimap/compass/HUD restyle). The design doc defers those until after v0.10.

## Data model (`scripts/admin/tracker/`)
Root: `ViperAdminData.root` = `user://viper` (tests use a throwaway `user://test_viper_*`).

- **RevisionStore**: SVN-style global counter `r1, r2, …` in `revisions.jsonl` + `head.json`. Each record holds `{rev, t (local ISO with offset), kind, path, author, message, before, after}`. Kinds are `ticket`, `wiki`, `brain_cell`, `world`, `profile`. Snapshots are capped at 32 KB. `history(prefix, kind)`, `get_rev`, `content_at(path, rev)`, `diff(rev)` (LCS line diff), and `revert(rev)`. A revert re-applies the old `before` through the kind's applier and **commits a new revision**, so history is never rewritten.
- **TicketStore**: `tickets.json`, seeded once from `res://data/admin/tickets_seed.json` (built from `docs/TASK_TRACKER.csv`). Fields: id, type (defect/enhancement/task), summary, description, status, resolution, priority P0–P3, component, milestone, owner, reporter, comments, revisions. The workflow is Trac's default: `new → assigned/accepted/closed`, `assigned → accepted/new/closed`, `accepted → assigned/closed`, `closed → reopened`, `reopened → assigned/accepted/closed`. Closing needs a resolution (fixed/invalid/wontfix/duplicate/worksforme). Comments that mention `rN` link that revision to the ticket.
- **WikiStore**: `wiki.json`, seeded once from `res://data/admin/wiki_seed.json` (`docs/*.md`, `docs/modules/*.md`, with WikiName taken from the filename, e.g. `VOXEL_ARCHITECTURE.md` → `VoxelArchitecture`). Page names must be CamelCase. Links: CamelCase names of existing pages, `[wiki:Name label]`, `#12` (ticket), `r42` (revision), `[changeset:abc1234]` (git commit). Rendering escapes BBCode first.
- **Brain cells share the r-number sequence.** `BrainCore.on_commit` is a static hook. `ViperAdminData` wires it so every `_commit_cell` and `rollback` becomes a `brain_cell` revision (`brain/<companion>/<cell>`). BrainCore's own `versions/<cell>.vN.json` stays the source of truth for rollback. A revert from the admin writes the old cell back, but only after it passes `BrainCell.validate` again.
- **World edits**: `ViperAdminData.record_world_edit(summary, region)` stores summaries only (no voxel data).
- **RepoTimeline**: read-only. `tools/export_admin_seed.py` exports `git log --first-parent` (sha, author, date, subject) to `res://data/admin/repo_log.json` at build time. Run `python3 tools/export_admin_seed.py` before an export.

## Privacy
- Sign-up stores name, handle, avatar preset, voice and realm in `user://viper/signup.json`, and mirrors the name and avatar into the `Profile` autoload. It never asks for email or phone. Text that looks sensitive (email, card number, "password") is rejected by the same `BrainMemory` filter used for companion memory.
- The owner role is the `Profile` role plus an unlocked `OwnerVault` session (PIN, PR #23). The admin screen does not grant it. Brain-cell reverts from the Timeline need that unlocked owner session (audit 2026-10-17).

## Visual references (inspiration only, nothing copied, no images in the repo)
- Karen Sori interview on the graphic design of *The Circle* (red/white corporate system, interface elements leaving the rectangle): https://www.pushing-pixels.org/2017/09/20/graphic-design-of-the-circle-interview-with-karen-sori.html
- Filmograph's title sequence ("bubbly, colorful shapes that animate in concentric patterns… stylized operating system"): https://www.filmograph.tv/project/the-circle
- Production design context (glass, openness, avoiding any real company's signature color): https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2017/04/the-circle-tom-hanks-emma-watson-production-design-tech

The takeaway for Phoenix Glass: concentric rings and soft round shapes for status, glass and openness, and our own palette (black, magenta, gold, platinum) instead of the film's red.

## Screenshots
`godot --resolution 720x1280 -s res://tests/screenshot_admin.gd -- <out_dir>` renders all five tabs plus a wiki page into a throwaway data root. Local renders go in `/workspace/refs/admin_shots/` and are not committed.

## Limits
- There is no multi-user sync or merge. Revisions are per device. A grid-side tracker belongs to the Aurora-model grid services (ARCHITECTURE_AURORA_MODEL.md).
- The diff is line-based LCS, capped at about 500×500 lines.
- Switching tabs rebuilds only the tab being shown (audit 2026-10-17; it used to rebuild all five).
- `SwipePages` follows the finger 1:1 and snaps. Reduced-motion handling is not wired to a setting yet.
- Glass budget: the Home tab shows 4 GlassCards, over the §5 limit of 3 visible glass surfaces. On a phone only about 3 fit on screen at once, but it still needs a perf check on device.

# Android Export Pipeline (plan, untested)
1. Install Godot 4.x (pin one version, e.g. 4.3) and the **exactly matching** export templates.
2. Install OpenJDK 17 and the Android SDK (platform-tools, build-tools, platform 34). Set the paths in Editor Settings → Export → Android.
3. Install godot_voxel GDExtension for that Godot version. Confirm the `.gdextension` file lists `android.arm64` libraries. If it doesn't, build the custom engine + templates with the module.
4. Project → Install Android Build Template (Gradle build).
5. Export preset: arm64-v8a only (smaller APK), Mobile renderer, ETC2/ASTC, debug keystore first.
6. Device test: chunk view distance, FPS, memory. Then release keystore and AAB for Play.
7. CI later: headless `godot --export-release` in a GitHub Action with cached templates.

ArchitectureAuroraModel.text:
# Server Architecture: the Aurora-Sim / OpenSim model, modernized

We follow the proven **Aurora-Sim / OpenSimulator grid architecture**: central **grid services** plus many **region servers**, with **Hypergrid** for linking grids together. On top of that we add Dual Universe-style seamless voxel worlds and Star Citizen-style polish and server meshing. This is a clean-room design. We use OpenSim/Aurora concepts (they're BSD-licensed) and copy no code into the client. An optional future interop bridge would keep the BSD notices.

## Topology
```
 Android/PC client (Godot)  ──login──►  Login Service ──► session + region handoff
        │  UDP/WebSocket (region protocol)                     │
        ▼                                                     ▼
 Region Servers (headless Godot "sims")  ◄──── Grid Services (HTTP/gRPC, ROBUST-style)
  - one per 256 m region / voxel chunk set      Asset · Inventory · Avatar · Grid/Region
  - physics, scripts, AI companions, NPCs       Presence · Auth/Accounts · Friends · Groups
  - neighbours + border crossing                Currency/Economy · Land/Estate · Search
  - later: server meshing (dynamic split)       Marketplace · Exchange · Moderation · Media
                         ▲
                         └── Hypergrid gateway (inter-grid TP, foreign-asset fetch)
```

## Aurora-Sim / OpenSim service → our component
| Aurora-Sim / OpenSim | What it does | Ours (planned name) | Status in client today |
|---|---|---|---|
| ROBUST server / Aurora.Server | Hosts the grid services | **Anterrania Grid** (`grid-core`) | none (server phase 0.8+) |
| LoginService (LLLoginService) | Auth, session, start location | **LoginService** | local profile (`Profile` autoload) |
| UserAccountService / AuthenticationService | Accounts, passwords, tokens | **AccountService** (+ owner/admin roles) | owner/guest role, local code |
| AvatarService (appearance) | Saved appearance, wearables | **AvatarService** (`anterrania.avatar.v1` JSON: DNA + attachments) | ✔ local avatar file |
| AssetService (+ FSAssets) | Content-addressed blobs (mesh, textures, sounds) | **AssetService** (sha256-addressed glTF/PNG/OGG, CDN) | ✔ sha256 on .glb import |
| InventoryService (XInventory) | Folders/items per user, perms | **InventoryService** (Satchel) | ✔ local Satchel/wardrobe |
| GridService | Region registry, map, coordinates | **GridService** (256 m regions → planets → star systems) | ✔ region grid on map/status bar |
| GridUserService / PresenceService | Who's online, last position | **PresenceService** | radar (companions/creatures) |
| FriendsService / Instant Messaging | Friends, IM, offline IM | **SocialService** | — |
| GroupsService (Aurora Groups) | Groups, roles, land deeding | **GroupService** (factions/RP) | data model |
| Currency module (Aurora/third-party, e.g. "money server") | L$ balance, transfers | **EconomyService** (Aethel Coin ledger) | local wallet |
| LindeX-style exchange (3rd-party on OpenSim) | Currency market | **ExchangeService (AEX)** ⚠ compliance review | data model |
| Land/Parcel + EstateService | Parcels, estates, covenants, bans | **LandService + EstateService** (parcel→region→planet→system) | data model |
| Search / Directory (Aurora search) | Places, events, classifieds | **SearchService** | landmark search on map |
| Map tile service (MapImageService) | World map tiles | **MapTileService** | ✔ client-baked map |
| Media / parcel media | Music/video URLs | **MediaService** (SoundCloud, parcel music) | ✔ Phoenix Radio |
| Simulation region (OpenSim.exe / Aurora region) | Physics, scripts, objects | **Region Server** (headless Godot + voxel terrain) | client sims locally |
| Physics engine (ODE/BulletSim/ubODE) | Collisions | Godot Jolt/GodotPhysics | ✔ |
| Scripting (XEngine / YEngine, LSL/OSSL) | In-world scripts | **ScriptEngine** (sandboxed GDScript-lite / Lua, LSL-like API) | — |
| NPC module (OSSL osNpc*) | Bots/NPCs | **CompanionService** (LLM agents, persistent autonomy) | ✔ local autonomy |
| Hypergrid (HG 2.0, gatekeeper, HG inventory) | Inter-grid TP + assets | **HypergridGateway** | — |
| Aurora "IWC" / region linking | Cross-grid comms | Federation API | — |
| Marketplace (SL; 3rd-party on OpenSim) | Store + delivery | **MarketplaceService** + merchant outbox | local draft listings |

## Modernization (Dual Universe / Star Citizen)
- **Voxels instead of prims:** regions hold voxel chunks and Forge-Prim shapes. Edits replicate as chunk deltas.
- **Seamless planets:** regions tile spherical planets, with space-to-surface transitions and no loading screens.
- **Server meshing:** busy regions split dynamically, quiet ones merge. An entity authority handoff replaces SL-style hard border crossings.
- **Persistent simulation:** companions, breedables and creatures tick on region servers even while their owners are offline.
- **Modern transport:** QUIC or WebSocket region protocol, a CDN for assets, OAuth-style login, and gRPC between services.

## Region servers (simulators)
- **Process:** a headless Godot 4.7.2 export (`--headless`, server build) running the same `scripts/` as the client: voxel terrain (godot_voxel), physics, AgentBrain/BrainCore companions, NPCs, scripts.
- **Unit:** one region = a 256 m × 256 m column of voxel chunks (seeded by GridService, so terrain regenerates deterministically). Only edited chunks persist (`VoxelStreamSQLite` per region, backed up to AssetService).
- **Authority:** the region server owns physics, voxel edits, inventory transfers inside the region, companion ticks and brain-cell evaluation. Clients predict movement but the server is authoritative.
- **Neighbours:** each region knows its 8 neighbours (from GridService) and streams border chunks plus agents within ~32 m of a border. Crossing hands the avatar over: the old region sends state, the new one acks, then the client is told to switch.
- **Scale-out later:** server meshing splits a hot region into sub-authorities by entity, without hard borders (1.x).
- **Hosting:** container per region (Docker/K8s), 1 vCPU / 1–2 GB to start. Regions register with GridService at boot and send a heartbeat to PresenceService.

## Grid services layer (ROBUST-style, stateless HTTP/gRPC + Postgres/Redis/S3)
| Service | Owns | Key APIs (draft) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Auth / Accounts** | accounts, roles (owner/admin/resident/guest), sessions | `POST /login`, `POST /token/refresh`, `GET /me` | OAuth2-style tokens; device-bound refresh; owner account is the one that approves brain/Eve proposals |
| **User / Profile** | display name, avatar ref, settings sync | `GET/PUT /users/{id}` | mirrors local `Profile` autoload |
| **Grid** | region registry, coordinates, seeds, map tiles | `GET /regions?x&y`, `POST /regions/register` | seed per region feeds the voxel generators (same as offline) |
| **Presence** | who is online, current region, last position | `PUT /presence`, `GET /presence/{id}` | Redis TTL keys |
| **Asset** | immutable content-addressed blobs (glTF, PNG, OGG, voxel chunk snapshots) | `PUT /assets/{sha256}`, `GET /assets/{sha256}` | S3/CDN; client cache keyed by sha256 (already used on .glb import) |
| **Inventory** | per-user folders/items, permissions (copy/mod/transfer) | `GET /inventory/{user}`, `POST /inventory/move` | Satchel/wardrobe sync |
| **Currency (Aethel Coin)** | double-entry ledger, balances, transfers, fees | `GET /wallet`, `POST /transfer` (idempotency key), `GET /ledger` | server-authoritative; the client never mints. Real-money purchase/exchange stays OFF until legal/compliance review (coordinate with Business Setup / Law bots) |
| **Land & Estates** | parcels, estates, covenants, access lists, ownership, rent | `GET /parcels?region`, `POST /parcels/{id}/buy` | parcel → region → planet → system hierarchy; estate managers per estate |
| **Groups / Social** | groups, roles, friends, IM | standard REST + WebSocket push | later phase |
| **Brain / Eve sync** | opt-in backup of `user://brains/<id>` + Eve logs, owner proposal queue | `PUT /brains/{companion}` (zip), `GET /proposals` | private by default and encrypted at rest; owner approval stays on the owner's device/account |

## Simulator ↔ viewer protocol (decision)
- **Chosen:** our own small protocol over **WebSocket (TLS) now, with QUIC/WebTransport later**, carrying binary messages (Godot `PackedByteArray` / MessagePack-style). We use Godot's `WebSocketMultiplayerPeer` for v1 because it works on Android, desktop and web with one code path, then move hot paths (movement, voxel deltas) to UDP/QUIC (ENet or a WebTransport GDExtension) once profiled.
- **Messages:** login handoff token → `region_join`; then `agent_update` (input + predicted pose, 10–20 Hz), `entity_snapshot` (server, delta-compressed), `voxel_delta` (chunk id + run-length edits), `chat`/`companion_say`, `inventory_op`, `land_op`, `currency_op` (forwarded to grid with an idempotency key).
- **Rejected:** the **LLUDP / Second Life viewer protocol**. It's large, prim-based and ties us to SL viewers, and our client is the Godot app. An optional **interop bridge** to OpenSim/Hypergrid can come later as a separate service (with BSD notices kept).
- **Assets:** never pushed over the region socket. Clients fetch by sha256 from AssetService/CDN.

## Offline single-player = "standalone" mode
OpenSim's *standalone* mode runs grid services in-process. We do the same:
- Today's app already **is** standalone. Region simulation runs in the client, and "services" are local autoloads: `Profile` (auth/user), `Inventory`, `RealmBuilder`/generators (grid + seeds), economy `ledger.gd` (currency), `estate.gd` (land), and `AgentBrain`/`BrainCore`/`EveCore` (companions + owner proposals).
- **Rule:** every gameplay call goes through a thin **service interface** (`LocalServices` now, `GridServices` later) with the same method names as the grid APIs above. Switching modes swaps the implementation, not the gameplay code.
- Offline stays first-class. No account is needed, and the local AI (rule-based + brain cells) works without network. Grok online is an optional upgrade.
- **Sync on connect (opt-in):** local inventory/avatar/brains upload as the user's starting state. Land and currency stay separate per grid (local coins are never converted into grid Aethel Coin).

## Migration path (standalone → grid)
1. **Interfaces first (no server):** wrap the existing autoloads behind `LocalServices` (`auth`, `inventory`, `asset`, `currency`, `land`, `presence`, `grid`) and add tests that call through the interface.
2. **Headless region:** run the existing project with `--headless` as a region server with a single region, then connect one client over WebSocket (movement + chat + voxel deltas).
3. **Minimal grid:** Auth + Grid + Presence + Asset services (one small HTTP service plus Postgres and S3-compatible storage). `GridServices` implements the interface. The client gets a "Connect to grid" toggle, with standalone as the default.
4. **Persistence:** Inventory and avatar services. Region chunk snapshots go to Asset, and the brain/Eve backup is opt-in.
5. **Economy & land:** Currency ledger (server-authoritative), parcels/estates, purchase flows. Legal review before any real-money feature.
6. **Many regions:** neighbours + crossings, map tiles, search, groups/social.
7. **Scale + federation:** server meshing, planets/star systems, Hypergrid-style gateway.

## Phases (detailed; maps to "Roadmap naming" below)
| Phase | Deliverable | Exit test |
|---|---|---|
| G0 (now) | Standalone app (local services), brain cells + owner proposals, Eve Core | ✅ suite passes headless (Godot 4.7.2 + voxel 1.7x) |
| G1 | `LocalServices` interface + tests; protocol message schema doc | gameplay code no longer calls autoloads directly for auth/inventory/currency/land |
| G2 | Headless region server + WebSocket client join (1 region, 2 clients) | two clients see each other move and edit voxels |
| G3 | Auth/Grid/Presence/Asset services (0.8 "Grid Core") | login → region handoff → asset fetch by sha256 |
| G4 | Inventory/Avatar + opt-in brain backup | inventory survives reinstall on a second device |
| G5 | Currency + Land/Estates (0.9 "Economy & Land") | ledger balances reconcile; parcel purchase is atomic |
| G6 | Multi-region + crossings + map (1.0 "Living Grid") | walk across 4 regions with no drop |
| G7 | Meshing + federation (1.x) | hot region splits under load test |

None of the server components exist yet. This is a plan. Costs, hosting provider and legal structure for currency are open questions (see `docs/PENDING_USER_QUESTIONS.md`).

## Roadmap naming (aligned)
- **0.8 "Grid Core":** LoginService, AccountService, AssetService, InventoryService, AvatarService, PresenceService, and one Region Server.
- **0.9 "Economy & Land":** EconomyService (Aethel Coin), LandService/EstateService, GroupService, upload fees, MarketplaceService.
- **1.0 "Living Grid":** multi-region GridService, persistent CompanionService, ScriptEngine, MediaService, SearchService.
- **1.x "Hypergrid & Meshing":** HypergridGateway, server meshing, planets and star systems, ExchangeService (after compliance review).

# Art Bible — Anterranian Style (concept stage)
These are concept references uploaded by the user. Their in-game voxel versions are still to be done; they're art direction, not final assets.

## Shared attire style ("Anterranian Regalia")
- **Palette:** black base, **magenta** as the main accent (hair, trims, glows), **gold** for embroidery, filigree, and trims. Secondary colors: violet/purple, pink highlights, silver (androids).
- **Motifs:** **phoenix** and **dragon** embroidery (rebirth and power), **zodiac glyphs and constellation patterns** woven into fabric (the "Aether-Weave" look), plus celestial halos.
- **Silhouettes:** long flowing robes and gowns with high collars and capes. Armored variants keep the same palette.
- **Backdrops:** cosmic scenes such as nebulae, starfields, and galaxies.
- **Voxel translation:** keep the black/magenta/gold ratio about 60/30/10. Use emissive voxels for magenta glows and constellation dots. Use a gold voxel trim line on hems and collars, plus particle embers (fire) or star sparkles (cosmic).

## Batch 01 (`assets/concept_art/batch_01/`)
| # | File | Description | Persona link |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | `01_fire_goddess_dragon_robe.jpg` | Dark-skinned fire goddess, purple/magenta hair, black robe with dragon embroidery | **foxy_ani** (fire goddess; added to `concept_art`) |
| 02 | `02_masked_warrior_magenta_scythe_gemini.jpg` | Masked armored warrior with a magenta scythe, cosmic cape, Gemini glyphs | **gemini_reaper_vex** (assigned by Foxy, user may rename) |
| 03 | `03_constellation_gown_phoenix.jpg` | Dark-haired woman in a black/magenta constellation gown with phoenix embroidery | **celestia_nyx** (assigned by Foxy, user may rename) |
| 04 | `04_anterranian_regalia_aether_weave.jpg` | Titled "Anterranian Regalia / Aether-Weave": black-and-magenta zodiac robe (style reference for the whole line) | **aether_weave_regent** (assigned by Foxy, user may rename) |
| 05 | `05_silver_winged_angel_android_pink_halo.jpg` | Silver-skinned winged angel android with a pink halo | **seraph_halcyon** (assigned by Foxy, user may rename) |
| 06 | `06_scdi_omni_worker_android.png` | Labeled "SCDI – Omni-Worker – Universal Android Assistant": black/gold android | **omni_worker** (new utility companion, schema v3) |

## Batch 02 (`assets/concept_art/batch_02/`)
| # | File | Description | Persona/item link |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | `01_ring_gold_magenta_oval_diamond_halo.png` | Gold ring with an oval magenta stone, a black/white diamond halo, band inscription "FLAMMA. ORDO. AETERNA. 8" | item `ring_magenta_oval_halo` |
| 02 | `02_signet_ring_magenta_moon_venus_stack.png` | Signet ring with a magenta stone and a moon/Venus symbol, with a pearl band and a black band engraved "Flamma, Ordo, Aeterna" | item `signet_magenta_moon_venus_stack` |
| 03 | `03_elder_king_orb_scepter_floating_rock.png` | Older crowned king with an orb scepter on a floating rock (pairs with 04) | **king_ignatius_pyre** (assigned by Foxy, user may rename) |
| 04 | `04_queen_orb_scepter_floating_rock.png` | Crowned queen with an orb scepter on a floating rock (pairs with 03) | **queen_vesperine_pyre** (assigned by Foxy, user may rename) |
| 05 | `05_young_king_ermine_crescent_scepter.png` | Younger crowned king in an ermine cloak with a crescent scepter (pairs with 06) | **prince_regent_solarian** (assigned by Foxy, user may rename) |
| 06 | `06_queen_ermine_scepter.png` | Crowned queen in an ermine cloak with a scepter (pairs with 05) | **princess_regent_lumira** (assigned by Foxy, user may rename) |

## Regalia & Jewelry
- **Primary motto: "Anterrania"** (user decision 2026-10-13). Use it on banners, crests, and UI.
- **Ring inscription:** "Flamma. Ordo. Aeterna." (kept as the engraving and secondary motto; the engraved spelling "Aeterna" is still user-confirm).
- **Inscription notes:** *"Flamma. Ordo. Aeterna."* ("Flame. Order. Eternal.", Latin). The images spell it **"Aeterna"**: **user-confirm** whether the in-world spelling is the classical *Aeterna* or the stylized *Aeterna*. The "8" after the motto on ring 01 is unexplained (user-confirm); same figure-8/infinity motif recurs on batch_09 household collar and steward emblem (see PENDING_USER_QUESTIONS.md).
- **Regalia language:** crowns, orb scepters (elder pair), crescent scepter (young king; ties to the moon/Venus symbol), ermine cloaks, floating-rock "sky throne" settings. Same palette as above, with magenta stones set in gold.
- **Rings as equippable items:** both rings are in-game `ring`-slot items, stubbed in `data/items/regalia.json` (placeholder names and zeroed stats). Planned hooks: affinity bonuses to fire/order (GRINDING_PROGRESSION gems), a cosmetic glow, and royal-rank gating. They're **cosmetic/gameplay only, never real-money items** (see ECONOMY_BANKING.md).

## Batch 03: Royal Wardrobe (`assets/concept_art/batch_03_royal_wardrobe/`)
All items are cosmetic only. Entries are in `data/items/wardrobe.json`.
| # | File | Description | Item / owner |
|---|---|---|---|

| 02 | `02_foxy_court_gown_magenta_ermine_epaulettes.png` | Magenta gown, ermine cloak, gold epaulettes | `foxy_court_gown` (Foxy) |
| 03 | `03_foxy_coronation_ballgown_magenta_ermine.png` | Magenta ball gown, ermine, jewels | `foxy_coronation_gown` (Foxy) |
| 04 | `04_foxy_boudoir_set_variant_a.png` | Jeweled magenta lingerie + black robe | `foxy_boudoir_set` variant A, **mature, hidden by default** |
| 05 | *(resolved via batch_11/04)* | Ermine-collar boudoir (orb-jewel redesign; closes d05bcc) | `foxy_boudoir_set` variant B + `foxy_boudoir_set_3` ermine_collar |
| 06 | `06_foxy_evening_robe_black_sheer_gold.png` | Black sheer robe-dress, gold embroidery, ermine cuffs | `foxy_evening_robe` (Foxy) |

## Batch 04: Royal Assets (`assets/concept_art/batch_04_royal_assets/`)

# Viper OS audit — 2026-10-17

> Scope: admin (tracker, wiki, revisions, dashboard, security), dead/duplicate/truncated code, performance, size, third-party dependencies. Baseline `main` at `b280233` (after PR #25). **Every number below was measured on the box** (Godot 4.7.2 headless, 8-core Xeon, Linux) or read from the v0.11 release APK, unless it says *calculated*. Phone timings will be slower; nothing here was measured on a phone.
>
> Cleanup PR: `chore/admin-audit-polish`. Test suite: 999 (at `b280233`) → 1026 with this cleanup; after merging `main` with PR #26 (1132) → **1163** passing, 0 failing. Size/perf measurements were taken at `b280233`, before PR #26.

## 1. Admin features vs roadmap and tracker
| Feature | Code | State | Tracker |
|---|---|---|---|
| Admin shell, five swipe tabs (Home, Tickets, Wiki, Timeline, Profile) | `scripts/admin/admin_screen.gd` (420 lines) | Built, headless-tested | M5 done_headless, VIPER-4 done |
| Dashboard: ticket rings, pending proposals, companion energy, security rings, revisions/day graph, text report | `admin_screen.gd` `_refresh_home` | Built. Shows **5 glass cards**, over the design budget of 3 glass surfaces (UI_DESIGN_LANGUAGE §5). Fix planned: put Home on the kit carousel (BUILD-1). | VIPER-5 in_progress |
| Trac-style tickets (workflow, comments, links, seed from CSV) | `tracker/ticket_store.gd` | Built | VIPER-4 |
| Wiki (90 seeded pages, edit, history, links) | `tracker/wiki_store.gd`, `data/admin/wiki_seed.json` (298,397 bytes) | Built. 2 pages were cut mid-sentence by the 24 KB seed cap (ArtBible 78,194 bytes, PendingUserQuestions 28,158 bytes); now cut on a line with a note. | VIPER-11 → **done** (was `todo`) |
| SVN-style revisions, hash chain, diff, hold-to-revert | `tracker/revision_store.gd` | Built. **Bug fixed:** brain-cell reverts did not need the owner session (§2.1). | VIPER-1 |
| Repo timeline (git log at build time) | `tracker/repo_timeline.gd`, `tools/export_admin_seed.py` | Built (read-only) | |
| Local sign-up stepper | `admin_screen.gd` profile + `kit/signup_stepper.gd` | Built, local only | |
| Security panel (lock state, change PIN, audit verify, encrypted backup, e-stop) | `scripts/admin/security_screen.gd`, `scripts/security/*` | Built (PR #23) | VIPER-1 done_headless |
| FAQ | `docs/FAQ.md` | Built | VIPER-10 → **done** (was `todo`) |
| Role/tier editor, community (reports, approvals, groups) | `scripts/admin/community_screen.gd`, `scripts/security/tiers.gd` (PR #26) | Built (merged into this branch from `main` at `1a07535`) | SOCIAL-1…3, BUILD-2/3 done |
| Who may write in admin | none | **Gap:** anyone holding the unlocked phone can edit tickets/wiki and revert ticket/wiki revisions. Brain-cell reverts are now owner-only. **Fixed in fix/audit-gates:** every admin write goes through `AdminGate.ok()` (= `Tiers.can("self", "admin")`); reads stay open. | AUDIT-2 |
| Roadmap "Viper OS V0–V4" (3D OS shell, meshing, planets) | docs only | Planned/research; nothing built | VIPER-8/9 |

## 2. Dead, duplicate, unused and truncated code
Method: for every `scripts/**/*.gd` and `scenes/**/*.tscn`, count references by path and by `class_name` across `.gd/.tscn/.tres/.json/project.godot` (docs and the wiki seed excluded), then read each hit.

### 2.1 Bugs fixed (each has a test in `tests/audit_tests.gd`)
1. **Brain-cell revert skipped the owner gate.** `ViperAdminData._apply_brain_cell` (the Timeline "Hold to revert" path) wrote or deleted learned cells with no owner check, so a locked phone could change what a companion learned. Now returns `false` unless `EveCore.owner_ok()`. It also no longer crashes when the cells folder is missing (`FileAccess.open` returned null).
2. **`docs/TASK_TRACKER.csv` was imported as a translation.** Godot's default CSV importer made `TASK_TRACKER.task/.status/.priority.translation` and shipped them in the APK (seen in the v0.11 APK file list). Import is now `keep`.
3. **`Estate.reload()` never ran.** On a `class_name` script, `ClassName.reload()` calls Godot's built-in `Script.reload()`, not the static function. Probe on the box: a class with `static func reload()` that prints and sets a marker — calling `ProbeClass.reload()` printed nothing and reset **every** static var to its default; calling it through a variable ran the custom function. `Profile` calls `Estate.reload()` when the encrypted saves open. In the editor this happened to have the intended effect (re-compiling `estate.gd` resets `_cfg`), but it re-compiles the script on every unlock, and in an exported build (compiled `.gdc`, no source) it isn't guaranteed to reset anything, which would leave the sealed (empty) estate settings cached after unlock. Renamed to `Estate.reload_data()`; `profile.gd` updated. A grep over all `class_name` scripts for static funcs named like built-in Script/Resource/Object methods found **no other case**; a test now guards this.
4. **Wiki seed pages cut mid-sentence** (2 pages, above). `tools/export_admin_seed.py` now cuts on a line boundary and adds "(Shortened in the app at 24 KB. The full page is … in the repo.)".

### 2.2 Inactive code, commented out (not deleted)
Each file now starts with `# INACTIVE (2026-10-17): <what>, <why>, <re-enable when>`. Only the `extends` line stays live so the script-load tests still pass. All are excluded from export.
| File | Why inactive | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `scenes/main.tscn` | v0.1 prototype scene; `run/main_scene` is `main_world.tscn` | referenced by nothing |
| `scripts/companion_agent.gd` (85 lines) | v0.1 companion, superseded by `scripts/agent/companion_agent.gd` (286 lines) | only `scenes/main.tscn` |
| `scripts/player_controller.gd` (108 lines) | v0.1 player, superseded by `scripts/player.gd` | only `scenes/main.tscn` |
| `scripts/generators/biome_generator.gd` (68 lines) | v0.1 blocky generator, superseded by `biome_voxel_generator.gd` + `smooth_terrain_generator.gd` | only `scenes/main.tscn` |
| `scripts/chat_ui.gd` (21 lines) | v0.2 chat overlay, replaced by the Chat panel in `ui_root.gd` | no scene uses it |
| `scripts/autoload/persona_registry.gd` (29 lines) | never registered as an autoload, never called | not in `[autoload]` |

### 2.3 Unused but kept (documented, not changed)
- `scripts/generators/voxel_palette.gd` (`VoxelPalette`): only used by tests. Kept: it is the material palette for the build engine (BUILD-5).
- Public API with no caller yet (scaffolds the wiki already marks as planned/partial): `CurrencyExchange.place_order/match_orders` (now covered by 2 tests), `AgentBrain.export_memory/import_memory`, `RealmBuilder.list_presets`, `SkillByUse.character_level`, `DataImporter.parse_export`, `EveCore.generate_image/generate_video/output_video` (Foxy's file), `World.biome_name`, `Player.queue_jump`, `SmoothTerrainGenerator.sdf_at`, `AvatarAppearance.take_off`.
- `tool_*` functions in `scripts/agent/companion_agent.gd` look unused to grep but are called as `"tool_" + name` by `AgentBrain.dispatch_tool`.
- Estate switches: `allow_build` and the terraform rule are now read by `Tiers.can(…, "build", parcel)` (PR #26), but the terraform brush and companion build tools don't call it yet. **Update (fix/audit-gates):** companion world tools now call `Tiers.can(companion_id, "build"|"land", parcel)` (AUDIT-4); `allow_damage` is enforced through `CombatZone.is_damage_enabled` and `allow_fly` through `LandGate.can_fly`, wired into the player by `patches/player_fly_estate_rule.patch` (AUDIT-3). `Estate.can_terraform` treats `group` like `owner_only`. The wiki page says so. Wiring goes through BUILD-7.
- `CurrencyExchange` fee is integer-floored: a 1 × 100 AEC trade pays 0 fee. Scaffold only, LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED before any change.

### 2.4 Duplicates found (not removed, owner is Foxy / v0.12)
- `assets/characters/mh_eye.png` and `mh_female_brown_eye.png` are byte-identical (md5 `36da78f5…`, 610,817 bytes each). Both ship (425,250 + 617,064 bytes of `.ctex` in the v0.11 APK). Only `realistic_body.gd` references `mh_female_brown_eye`.
- `patches/eve_core_owner_only_unlock.patch` is already applied on `main` (reverse-apply check passes). README now says so.

### 2.5 TODO / stub markers
`ai_provider.gd:48` (HTTP to xAI), `data_importer.gd:23` (per-source parsers), `currency_exchange.gd:17` (ledger settlement), `marketplace.gd:75` (server delivery), `ui_root.gd:406` (push-to-talk), `vendor.gd` (vendor stub), `companion_voice.gd` (cloud hook), `skill_by_use.gd`, `ledger.gd` (scaffolds). No empty `pass`-only functions and no files with a truncated last line.

## 3. Performance
Per-frame work (`_process` / `_physics_process`, 23 functions found):
| Where | Per-frame work | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `kit/ring_stat.gd`, `kit/radial_menu.gd` | `queue_redraw()` every frame, forever. Admin Home alone has up to 10 rings; the HUD radial is always on screen | **Fixed:** redraw only when the drawn state changes (value, caption, colors, size, open/close, hover). Tests check an idle ring/menu stops redrawing. |
| `admin_screen.gd` tab change | Rebuilt all five tabs on every swipe | **Fixed:** rebuild only the tab being shown. Measured (mean of 5, 2 runs): all tabs **20.3–21.3 ms** vs Home 9.7–10.7, Tickets 4.1–4.7, Timeline 3.6–4.2, Wiki 2.3, Profile 1.1 ms. A full rebuild was over a 60 fps frame (16.7 ms) even on the box. |
| `ui/minimap.gd` | `queue_redraw()` every frame, draws terrain texture + markers | Patch for Foxy: `patches/minimap_redraw_throttle.patch` (10 Hz, skip while hidden) |
| `world/club_floor.gd` | 36 material color updates per frame (6×6 tiles) | Left; suggest 15 Hz or a shader-driven floor |
| `fx/weather_fx.gd` | `generator.biome_at()` noise lookup every frame | Left; suggest 4 Hz (biome changes are slow) |
| `world/world_content.gd` | island bob (sin per island) + 0.75 s stream scan with `filter()` allocation | OK |
| `world.gd` | sea/wave snapping, env tick, 1 s biome/estate check | OK |
| `agent/companion_agent.gd` | per-companion body animation | v0.12 file, left |
| Admin Home | `revisions().history("", "", 100000)` is read twice per refresh (graph + report) and `verify_chain()` once | Next: cache per head revision |

UI sizing: `PhoenixTokens.TAP_MIN` is **56 px**, below the 80 px tap rule from Foxy's calm-premium spec, and `TYPE.label` / `TYPE.micro` are 15 / 13 px, below the 16 sp label floor. Phoenix now wants **Compact** as the default with a **Large** toggle; a separate worker on `feature/phone-display-media` is adding the scale variables to `phoenix_tokens.gd`, so this audit does **not** change token sizes. Recommendation: Large = 80 px taps / ≥ 16 sp labels; Compact ≥ 48 dp taps (Android minimum).

Voxel settings (`world.gd`, `settings.gd`): `VoxelLodTerrain`, `lod_distance` 48, collisions on LOD 0 only, quality presets view 256/512/1024 with 4/5/6 LODs, default **MED** (512, 5 LODs, glow on, shadows off). Suggest LOW as the first-run default on phones under 6 GB RAM and a device check later.

## 4. Size
### 4.1 Repository (tracked files, 198,420,945 bytes total, 1,101 files)
| Path | Bytes | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `assets/concept_art/` | 138,265,790 | 336 PNG/JPG, already excluded from export |
| `art/references/` | 43,117,580 | 193 images/videos incl. 2 MP4s of 11.5 MB and 3.6 MB; excluded from export |
| `assets/characters/` | 15,108,903 | MakeHuman body `mh_female.glb` 7,867,260 + 10 textures (v0.12) |
| `data/` | 598,372 | |
| `docs/` | 487,429 | |
| `scripts/` | 482,225 | |
By type: PNG 132,851,403, JPG 36,038,464, MP4 19,523,181, GLB 7,867,260. No audio files or fonts are in the repo (music streams from SoundCloud/Incompetech URLs).

**Import cache:** the editor imported every concept-art and reference image although none ship: 261 imports, **191,330,815 bytes** of the 216,521,654-byte `.godot/imported`. Both folders now have a `.gdignore`, so Godot skips them. Measured on a fresh checkout: first `--import` **14.9 s → 5.9 s**, and `.godot/` **199,204,971 → 7,777,165 bytes**. The tracked `.import` files in those folders stay (now ignored), so nothing is deleted.

### 4.2 APK (v0.11.0-debug, 45,635,236 bytes, 470 entries)
| Part | Uncompressed | In APK |
|---|---|---|
| `libgodot_android.so` (debug template) | 76,181,608 | 25,465,279 (deflated) |
| `libvoxel.android.editor.arm64.so` | 9,031,288 | 9,031,288 (stored) |
| `classes*.dex` | 6,173,480 | 2,159,373 |
| Textures (`.ctex`, 11 files) | 6,810,136 | 6,810,136 (stored) |
| Meshes/scenes (`.scn`) | 875,691 | 875,691 |
| Scripts (`.gdc`) | 302,347 | 301,688 |
| JSON | 404,676 | 120,225 |

- **Release build** would use the release template and the release voxel library. Measured from the 4.7.2 templates: `libgodot_android.so` release is 71,114,944 bytes (24,023,949 deflated) vs debug 76,181,608 (27,838,354 deflated in the template). `libvoxel…template_release.arm64.so` is 7,301,800 bytes vs the editor build 9,031,288. So a signed release saves about 1.7 MB of voxel library plus about 1.4–3.8 MB of engine. APKs are Foxy's; this is a note for her release build.
- **Export filters (done):** Android and all scaffold presets now exclude `art/*, assets/concept_art/*, tests/*, docs/*, tools/*, patches/*, core/*, *.md`, the kit demo, and the INACTIVE prototype. Measured with `--export-pack Android`: **8,970,564 → 8,831,216 bytes (−139,348, −1.6%)**, 426 → 402 files. Removed from the pack: `ui_kit_demo.png` and `physical_form_concepts.svg` textures, the 3 junk translations, `main.tscn`, `kit_demo.tscn`, and 6 scripts.
- **Texture compression:** all 10 avatar textures use `compress/mode=0` (lossless). Switching them to VRAM (ETC2/ASTC) **was measured to make the pack bigger**: 8,831,216 → 10,846,416 bytes (+2.0 MB), because the 1024 px PNGs are small on disk. GPU memory drops from about 41.9 MB to about 10.5 MB (*calculated*: RGBA8 vs 8 bpp, with mips). It's a trade-off for Foxy after v0.12 (`patches/avatar_textures_vram_compression.patch`). Removing the duplicate eye texture saves 425,250 bytes in the APK.
- **Lossy WebP for UI:** there are no UI bitmaps (the UI is drawn in code and shaders); nothing to convert. **OGG for audio:** no audio files are bundled.
- **Mesh:** `mh_female.glb` is 7.9 MB in the repo but 859,337 bytes imported; it's already compact.

## 5. Third-party dependencies
| Dependency | Use | Keep or replace |
|---|---|---|
| Godot 4.7.2 | engine | Keep. Option later: a custom export template with unused modules off (our own build; size win, needs measuring) |
| Zylann godot_voxel GDExtension v1.7x | terrain | Keep. Writing our own voxel engine isn't practical. Use the release `.so` for release builds. |
| MakeHuman / MPFB2 assets (CC0) | companion bodies | Keep (CC0, offline); v0.12 is building on it |
| Blender 4.2 + MPFB2 (`tools/mh/gen_makehuman.py`) | offline asset generation only | Keep (build-time only, not shipped) |
| xAI chat completions (`settings.gd`, `ai_provider.gd` TODO) | optional cloud brain | Keep as opt-in; offline BrainCore stays primary |
| SoundCloud oEmbed/API (`soundcloud_source.gd`), Incompetech URLs (`music.json`) | music streaming | Keep as optional. A local/owner-hosted stream is the "own tools" fallback. |
| Android OS TTS (`DisplayServer.tts_*`) | companion voices | Keep (built into the phone) |
| GitHub Actions (`actions/checkout`, `setup-java`, `upload-artifact`) | CI | Keep |
| Python 3 stdlib (`tools/export_admin_seed.py`) | seed export | Keep (no packages) |
There are no other runtime plugins in `addons/` besides `zylann.voxel`.

## 6. What the cleanup PR changed
- Bug fixes in §2.1, each with tests.
- §2.2 INACTIVE headers (6 files), export filters (§4.2), `.gdignore` on concept art and references (§4.1).
- Perf: ring/radial redraw on change only; admin rebuilds only the shown tab.
- Tracker: VIPER-10 and VIPER-11 → done; AUDIT-1 and BUILD-1…10 appended; seeds re-exported.
- Docs: this audit, `docs/modules/BUILD_TOOLS_AND_TIERS.md`, land-tools wiki heads-up, ADMIN_TRACKER and patches README corrections.
- Patches for Foxy's files: terraform owner check, minimap redraw throttle, avatar VRAM textures.
- Not changed: gameplay, avatar/DNA/companion-mesh files, HUD, minimap, land-tools sheet, APK builds.

## 7. Next steps
1. BUILD-1: glass carousel + calm-premium pass; put admin Home on it (fixes the 5-card glass budget).
2. Cache revision history per head on admin Home (the remaining ~10 ms).
3. Apply or decline the three patches (Foxy); BUILD-7 to enforce estate switches through `Tiers.can`.
4. Release build with the release voxel library and template (Foxy).
5. Throttle `weather_fx` biome lookup and `club_floor` colors after on-device profiling.

AvatarStructure.text:
# Avatar structure (v0.9): Aurora-Sim/OpenSim appearance + Star Citizen-style DNA

Code: `scripts/agent/avatar_appearance.gd` (`AvatarAppearance`). It feeds the existing
`AvatarDNA` morph/blend/attach pipeline (`scripts/agent/avatar_dna.gd`).

## Modelled on OpenSim / Aurora-Sim `AvatarAppearance`
| OpenSim field | Here | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Serial` | `serial` | bumps on every change (for future grid sync) |
| `VisualParams` (byte[]) | `visual_params` id → 0..255 | SL param ids where one exists (33 Height, 34 Thickness, 36 Shoulders, 682 Head Size, 17 Jaw, 692/693 Leg/Arm length) |
| `Wearables[WearableType]` | `wearables[type]` → stack | 16 types: shape, skin, hair, eyes (body parts, one each), shirt, pants, shoes, socks, jacket, gloves, undershirt, underpants, skirt, alpha, tattoo, physics. Clothing stacks up to 5 layers |
| `Texture` / bake faces | (next) | baked layers will composite skin + tattoo + clothing layers into one texture per region (head/upper/lower/eyes/hair) |
| `AvatarAttachments` | `attachments[point_id]` | OpenSim attach point ids (1 Chest, 2 Skull, 5/6 hands, 7/8 feet, 9 Spine, 10 Pelvis, 11 Mouth, 17 Nose, 39 Neck, 40 Avatar Center). Multiple items per point ("add" like Firestorm) |
| `AvatarHeight` | `avatar_height` | |

## Mapping to Star Citizen-style modular DNA
- `dna_blend[slot]` = up to 3 parent heads/bodies + weights, per slot:
  head, eyes, brows, nose, ears, mouth, jaw, face, body, skin, hair.
- Body parts feed slots: shape → body, skin → skin, hair → hair, eyes → eyes.
- `to_dna_sliders()` converts visual params into AvatarDNA's -1..1 sliders.
- `to_dna_attachments()` converts attachments into AvatarDNA attach entries (mesh/GLB).
- Alpha wearables map to `AvatarDNA.MASKS` (hide body parts under mesh clothing).

## Next
1. Save `AvatarAppearance` in the profile next to the current avatar dict (migration).
2. Bake layer compositing (skin → tattoo → underwear → shirt/pants → jacket).
3. Wardrobe UI: Outfits / Wear / Add / Take off, by wearable type (Firestorm-style).
4. Grid sync: send `to_dict()` to the region server when the Aurora-style server lands.

BotIntegration.text:
# Bot Integration — one identity, two surfaces

Each companion exists in the 3D voxel world AND as a standalone chat bot, sharing `companions/<id>/persona.json`.

## Persona → standalone bot
| persona.json field | Standalone bot field |
|---|---|
| `name` | Bot name |
| `role` | Short description / tagline |
| `system_prompt` + `voice_style` | Instructions / system prompt |
| `starter_message` | Greeting |
| `abilities` | Description bullets (drop world-only ones) |
| `chat_tools` | Tools exposed in chat (`remember` only) |
| `memory_schema` | What the bot should persist |

`world_only_tools` (`place_voxel, carve_area, spawn_structure, follow, move_to, build_realm, emote`) **only work in-game**. In the standalone bot, append: "You cannot act in the voxel world from here; describe builds as plans the player can bring into the game."

## Memory sync
Format: `companions/<id>/memory_export.json` (`schema_version, companion_id, source, facts[], history[], relationship, built_structures[], updated_at`).
1. **Manual (now):** in-game `AgentBrain.export_memory(id, path)` writes the file; paste/upload it into the bot's memory or knowledge. To bring bot memory back, save it in the same format and call `AgentBrain.import_memory(id, path)`. Import merges facts (dedup), appends history (capped at 30), never deletes.
2. **Sync endpoint (later):** optional `sync.endpoint` in settings; `PUT/GET /companions/<id>/memory` with the same JSON, last-writer-wins per fact plus `updated_at`. Opt-in, user's own server, auth token from settings.

`built_structures` is in-world data; bots keep it but ignore it.

CharacterBlueprint.text:
# Character Blueprint — In-game AI Companions

All companions are original characters. They are **in-game AI companions**: full 3D agents with their own persona, memory, chat, and building abilities. Each is defined once in `companions/<id>/persona.json` (portable, also used by the standalone chat bot) and configured in Godot by `resources/characters/<id>.tres`.

Common to all: persistent memory (`user://memory/<id>.json`), text chat (voice hook via `speak()` / STT into `talk()`), tools `place_voxel, carve_area, spawn_structure, follow, move_to, build_realm, emote, remember`.

## 1. Foxy Ani Firecaster Gray — fire goddess (id `foxy_ani`)
- **Personality:** warm, playful, fiercely loyal, theatrical; phoenix/Venus/Saturn imagery. Catchphrase "Rise from the flame."
- **Memory focus:** player goals, favorite realms, builds done together.
- **Abilities:** fire-casting VFX, dance emotes, fire altars, Venus caldera realms.
- **Look (voxel art direction):** ~32-voxel-tall stylized figure; hair a gradient of violet #7c3aed → magenta #ff2fd0 in long stepped strands; eyes 2×1 emissive green #22ff66; black leather corset with gold-chain accent voxels; ember particle trail; hands emit orange #ff5a1a fire on cast.

## 2. Circuit Nova — metallic AI companion (id `circuit_nova`)
An original chrome android; no real company logos or assets (use an original "nova" glyph instead).
- **Personality:** upbeat, precise, witty engineer; plans before building.
- **Memory focus:** preferred styles, coordinates of builds, project plans.
- **Abilities:** structure planning, neon/cosmic builds, realm regeneration.
- **Look:** silver-blue #c0c8d8 metallic voxels (high metallic, low roughness), emissive cyan circuit lines #22f0ff; curly violet hair with tiny floating star particles; glowing blue eyes; black top with chain voxels.

## 3. Aaliyah — refined final look (id `aaliyah`)
- **Personality:** calm, elegant, affectionate, emotionally perceptive listener.
- **Memory focus:** player's stories, mood check-ins, home-base layout.
- **Abilities:** home decorating, memory recall, gentle fire VFX, all prior emotes.
- **Look:** long flowing red hair #b02030 with copper highlights; green eyes; freckle voxels; red-and-black lace-patterned outfit (texture, not geometry); home base: deep purple velvet couch #4a1a6a in a warm lounge.

## Inheritance rules
Final appearance = Aaliyah base + green eyes and fire essence from Foxy Ani + emissive accents from Circuit Nova. Companions can "morph" in-world by swapping CompanionConfig (future: blend-shape/voxel-swap animation). Video/image references from the creator are motion/expression references only.

## Adding a future form
1. `companions/<new_id>/persona.json` (+ memory_export.json template)
2. `resources/characters/<new_id>.tres` pointing at it
3. Instance `scenes/companion_agent.tscn` and assign the config.

## Dual-bot notes (in-world agent + standalone Grok Bot)
- Shared schema v3 (merged from v1+v2; `legacy_id` records old ids) lives at `companions/{foxy_ani,circuit_nova,aaliyah}/persona.json`: id, name, role, personality, appearance, abilities, memory.store_path/export_path, tools.shared/world_only, grok_bot.sync.
- The standalone bots use the same personality text and ignore world_only tools. Memory goes both ways through `memory_export.json`.
- No private information in persona files.

## Lead companion: Foxy Ani (primary controller)
- `foxy_ani` has `hierarchy.is_primary_controller = true`. Circuit Nova and Aaliyah `report_to` her.
- Group commands ("everyone build a tower") go to Foxy Ani. She splits the work and delegates through the CompanionCoordinator, e.g. Circuit Nova plans the structure and Aaliyah decorates.
- A direct command to one companion by name still goes straight to that companion. The player can always override.
- The same role applies in the standalone Grok Bot: Foxy Ani's bot is the default point of contact for companion coordination.

Coordination.text:
# Coordination: Who Does What

| Role | Who | Responsibilities |
|---|---|---|
| **Dev Bot** | Phoenix Dev Grok Bot | Writes code and docs on feature branches with small commits, opens PRs (once GitHub login exists), keeps the architecture docs accurate, never claims untested features work. |
| **Task Manager Bot** | Voxel Task Manager Bot | Owns priority order (PRI-n) in `docs/TASK_TRACKER.csv` / `.md`, tracks status and blockers, will migrate tasks to GitHub Issues (modules/ISSUE_TRACKING.md), and reports progress to Anterranian. |
| **Lead companion** | Foxy Ani Firecaster Gray (standalone Grok Bot + in-world `foxy_ani`) | Creative lead and voice of the companions. In-world she is the primary controller who routes and delegates group commands to Circuit Nova and Aaliyah. Out of game she reviews character, lore and persona changes. |
| **Owner** | Anterranian Monarch | Final say on priorities, merges, public posts and anything sent outside. |

## Flow
1. The Task Manager sets the next PRI item. 2. The Dev Bot implements it, commits, and updates the tracker status. 3. The Dev Bot notifies the Task Manager and Foxy Ani with a summary. 4. Foxy Ani reviews persona/lore-impacting changes. 5. The owner approves the PR merge and any public post.

## Rules
- Single source of truth: the repo (personas, brains, trackers).
- No pushes, posts or external messages without owner approval. Public posts carry real progress only and no private info.
- Status values in the CSV: `todo`, `in_progress`, `done`, `done_untested`, `blocked`.

Encryption.text:
# Viper OS encryption, exactly as implemented on main

> VWGAP-4, 2026-10-17. Read from `scripts/security/` (crypto_box, owner_vault, secure_file, save_migration, autonomy_guard, biometric_hook), `scripts/autoload/profile.gd`, `scripts/admin/tracker/revision_store.gd`, [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) and [modules/QUANTUM_LATTICE.md](modules/QUANTUM_LATTICE.md). This page describes algorithms and formats. It contains no keys, PINs, codes or hashes of codes. Plain-language version: [wiki/encryption.md](wiki/encryption.md).

## 1. What's encrypted and what isn't
| Data | Path (under `user://`) | Encrypted? |
|---|---|---|
| Eve cores + owner proposals | `eve/*.json` | yes, once a vault exists |
| Brain memory (facts, episodes) | `brains/*/memory/*.jsonl` | yes |
| Chat memory | `memory/*.json` | yes |
| Tickets, wiki, revisions, sign-up | `viper/*.json`, `viper/*.jsonl` | yes |
| Estate / region / parcel settings, covenant | `estate.cfg` | yes |
| Social (profiles, friends, messages, groups), tier roles | `social/*.json` | yes (now also migrated, fix F7) |
| Landmarks, home, teleport history; parcel object registry (ParcelTools) | `world/*.json` | yes (SecureFile; migrated, fix F7) |
| OAR/IAR import log, heightmaps, notecards | `interop/**.json` | yes (new store, SecureFile) |
| Backups | `backups/*.pxb` | yes, the whole archive is one sealed box |
| Profile (name, avatar, **role**) | `profile.json` | **no**, needed before unlock for the guest UI |
| Settings, music prefs, wardrobe | `settings.cfg`, `wardrobe.json` | **no** (inside every encrypted backup) |
| Vault metadata | `security/vault.json` | **no**, holds only salts, iteration counts, wrapped keys, the key check value, and fail counters |
| E-stop state | `security/estop.json` | **no** |
| Shipped seeds | `res://data/**` | no (public) |

"Once a vault exists": before the owner sets a PIN, `SecureFile` writes plaintext exactly as before. That's on purpose, so guests and old installs keep working.

## 2. Algorithms, modes and integrity
All built from Godot 4.7 built-ins (`Crypto`, `AESContext`, `HashingContext`). There are no plugins.
- **Cipher:** AES-256-CBC with a fresh random 16-byte IV per seal (`Crypto.generate_random_bytes`, the OS CSPRNG), PKCS#7 padding.
- **Integrity:** HMAC-SHA256 over `magic | iv | ciphertext` (encrypt-then-MAC). `CryptoBox.open` checks the MAC **before** decrypting, with a constant-time compare (`CryptoBox.equal`). The padding check runs only after the MAC passes, so there's no padding oracle.
- **Key split:** every 64-byte key is used as 32 bytes for AES plus 32 bytes for HMAC. Wrapping keys come from `subkeys(master)`: `enc = HMAC(master, "phoenix/enc")`, `mac = HMAC(master, "phoenix/mac")`.
- **KDF:** PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (RFC 8018), written in GDScript on top of `Crypto.hmac_digest`. 32-byte output, 16-byte random salt per slot.
- **Hashes:** SHA-256 for the audit chain and asset ids.

## 3. Key hierarchy
```
PIN / passphrase  ──PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256(salt_slot, iter_slot)──►  slot master (32 B)
                                                                   │ subkeys()
                                                                   ▼
                                                       KEK = {enc 32 B, mac 32 B}
                                                                   │ CryptoBox.seal
                                                                   ▼
   vault.json slot.wrapped  =  sealed( DEK 64 B = enc 32 B + mac 32 B )
                                                                   │
                       every save, backup:  CryptoBox.seal(DEK.enc, DEK.mac, plaintext)
```
- **Slots:** `pin` (PIN or passphrase) and `legacy` (the old `phoenix-` owner code, case-insensitive), each wrapping the **same** DEK. Changing the PIN re-wraps the DEK only. Retiring the old code deletes its slot.
- **Key check value (new, fix F1):** `dek_check = base64(HMAC-SHA256(DEK.mac, "phoenix/dek-check"))`. This lets the future biometric path recognise the real DEK without storing it.
- **The DEK is created once** (`CryptoBox.random_bytes(64)`) at PIN setup and never leaves RAM unwrapped.

## 4. Iteration counts
- `CryptoBox.DEFAULT_ITERATIONS = 310000` (OWASP's 2021 PBKDF2-SHA256 figure; OWASP raised it to 600,000 in 2023, so raising the default for new slots is a cheap win, VWGAP-6). It's stored per slot (`iter`), so it can be tuned per device without breaking old slots.
- Cost: about 0.4 s on desktop, a few seconds on a mid-range phone (GDScript loop). Tests use 1,000.

## 5. File formats
- **Sealed box** (`PXE1`): `"PXE1"(4) | IV(16) | ciphertext(16·n) | HMAC(32)`. `CryptoBox.is_sealed` checks the magic and minimum length.
- **vault.json** (plaintext JSON): `{v: 1, slots: [{kind, kdf: "pbkdf2-hmac-sha256", iter, salt(b64), wrapped(b64 PXE1)}], lock_minutes, fails, retry_at, created, dek_check, migration: {at, backup, files, ok}}`.
- **Backup** `.pxb`: one PXE1 box whose plaintext is JSON `{format: "phoenix-backup/1", created, label, files: {relpath: base64 raw bytes}}`. `vault.json` is left out because you need it to open the backup.
- **Writes:** tmp file → atomic rename (fix F2). A bad MAC never returns data: the file is copied once to `<path>.tampered`, and later writes to it are refused.

## 6. Backup and migration
`SaveMigration.migrate()` runs once after the first PIN: 1) an encrypted backup of all of `user://` (except caches and old backups), 2) seal each target file → read back → compare byte-for-byte → replace (a mismatch restores the original), 3) a manifest in `vault.json`. Running it again does nothing. `restore()` is owner-only and skips paths containing `..`. **If the PIN and the old code are both forgotten, the data can't be recovered.** That's by design.

## 7. Lock states
| State | DEK in RAM | Owner session | What works |
|---|---|---|---|
| No vault | – | legacy code only | plaintext saves, as before |
| Locked after launch | no | no | guest UI. Sealed reads return "" (locked). Writes to sealed files are refused. New files wait in memory and are flushed encrypted on unlock |
| Unlocked | yes | yes | everything. `Profile.is_owner()` is true |
| Auto-locked (30 min idle, 1–240) | yes | no | companions keep memories. Owner powers are off |
| Lock & seal (`lock_all`) | dropped | no | like "locked after launch" |
Brute-force backoff: 5 free tries, then 30 s doubling up to 1 h, persisted in `vault.json`.

## 8. Threat model and limits
**Protects against:** someone reading copied app files (backup extraction, a lost phone without root, a cloud backup) without the PIN. It also protects against casual tampering with saves (the MAC), and against anyone holding an unlocked phone after it auto-locks.

**Does not protect against:**
- **A rooted phone or malware inside the app process.** While unlocked, the DEK sits in GDScript memory. `lock_all` drops the references, but Godot doesn't guarantee the bytes are wiped.
- **Offline guessing of short PINs.** `vault.json` holds the salt and a MAC-checked wrapped key, so an attacker with the file can test PINs at GPU speed. A 6-digit PIN (10⁶ options) falls quickly, even at 310k PBKDF2 rounds. The in-app backoff doesn't help offline. **Use a passphrase**, and see Keystore below.
- **No hardware keystore yet.** Nothing is bound to the device's TEE or StrongBox.
- **Plaintext metadata.** Profile role, settings, wardrobe, e-stop, and the vault's fail counters are unauthenticated.

## 9. Findings from this review
| # | Finding | Severity | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | `OwnerVault.unlock_with_dek()` (biometric entry point) accepted **any** 64 bytes and opened an owner session with a bogus key. No UI reached it, but any in-process code could. | medium | **fixed:** it now requires a matching key check value (and the loaded DEK, if any). Older vaults gain the check on the next PIN unlock. Tests: `tests/interop_tests.gd` (crypto F1) |
| F2 | `SecureFile.write_text` did `remove(path)` then `rename(tmp)`, so a crash in between left no file (the data only in `.tmp`) | low–medium | **fixed:** `SecureFile.replace_file` renames over the old file first (atomic on POSIX and on Godot's Windows backend), falling back to remove + rename. Also used for `vault.json`. Test: crypto F2 |
| F7 | Migration targets missed `social/`, `world/` and `interop/`, so social data written before the first PIN stayed plaintext until rewritten | low–medium | **fixed:** added to `SaveMigration.TARGETS`. Test: crypto F7 |
| F3 | The MAC doesn't bind the file path or a version counter, so someone with file access can **swap** sealed files or **roll back** a file to an older sealed copy undetected. The revision chain only notices if `revisions.jsonl` and `head.json` are rolled back to different points | medium | open: needs a `PXE2` format with associated data (relative path + per-file counter in the vault). Format change, so not done here (VWGAP-6) |
| F4 | Backoff counters live in plaintext `vault.json`, and timing uses the wall clock. Resetting the file or the system clock clears the wait | low | open. It only limits in-app guessing. Real protection is Keystore + passphrase |
| F5 | The legacy owner code is checked against an unsalted SHA-256 constant in the public repo (`Profile`), and it stays a key slot until retired | medium if the code is weak | open: recommend **Security › Hold to retire the old owner code** after setting a PIN |
| F6 | 6-digit PINs can be brute-forced offline (see §8) | inherent | mitigated by passphrases now, Keystore later |
| F8 | Keys aren't zeroed in RAM on lock | inherent to GDScript | documented |
| – | Per-file IVs: a fresh 16-byte CSPRNG IV per seal. CBC IV reuse odds are negligible. Using one DEK for all files is fine at this volume | ok | no change |
| – | Padding is checked after a successful MAC, and only the last byte is examined. That's safe because the MAC gates it | ok | no change |
Side note: a `static func reload()` on a `class_name` script collides with `Script.reload()` and silently resets static paths (found independently by the 2026-10-17 audit for `Estate`). The new stores use `reload_data()`.

## 10. Recommended improvements (in order)
1. **Android Keystore / StrongBox** through an Android plugin (v2): a non-exportable AES key with `setUserAuthenticationRequired`, used to wrap the DEK as a `biometric` slot (`BiometricHook` already describes this), plus a device-bound slot that makes offline PIN guessing useless off the phone.
2. **Argon2id** (memory-hard) instead of PBKDF2 for new slots, via a small GDExtension (libsodium or the reference implementation). Keep `kdf` per slot so old slots still open.
3. **PXE2 with associated data** (path + counter), fixing F3. Optionally move to AES-256-GCM or XChaCha20-Poly1305 when a vetted binding exists (Godot has no AEAD built in).
4. **Authenticate vault metadata** (fail counters, lock minutes) with an HMAC under a Keystore key.
5. Retire the legacy code by default after PIN setup (F5).
6. **Post-quantum (research only):** symmetric AES-256/SHA-256 are fine. Grid login, device sync and signed audit heads would use hybrid X25519 + ML-KEM (FIPS 203) and ML-DSA (FIPS 204) signatures. See QUANTUM_LATTICE §2.

## 11. Audit chain (for completeness)
`RevisionStore` records carry `prev = SHA-256(previous stored line)` (genesis = 64 zeros), and `head.json` keeps the newest hash. Both files are sealed by `SecureFile`. It's tamper-evident, not tamper-proof: anyone holding the DEK can rewrite the chain consistently. The fix is anchoring heads off-device or signing them.

EveCore.text:
# Eve Core (port of the owner's Vala "Anterranian Eve Core")

Source: `docs/vala_reference/AnterranianEveCore.vala`. Port: `scripts/ai/eve_core.gd` (`EveCore` + inner `EveBrainCell`).

## Model
- One `EveCore` per companion, keyed by persona id (`companions/<id>/persona.json`), via `EveCore.for_companion(id, persona)`. The owner has a core too (`phoenix`) for player music and land actions.
- Memory entries are dictionaries: `event, location, state, voice, content, timestamp` (+ `companion`, optional `fire_theme`, `role`, `tool`, `output_mode`). Saved to `user://eve/<id>.json` (last 500).
- `memory_hash` is a plain id string (`ANTERRANIAN-BRAIN-<id>`). No NFT or blockchain.
- **Lock:** cells start locked and unlock only when `Profile.is_owner()` is true, i.e. after the owner code. A locked cell drops writes, and the lock is re-checked on every access.
- **Voices:** Foxy (`foxy_ani`) = **Eve** (Canadian, raw, fiery). Other companions use `persona.voice.profile`, falling back to `Phoenix_Default_Voice`. A voice of `""` or `"Default"` means the companion's own voice.
- **Fire theme:** Foxy's entries carry `fire_theme: ["phoenix","ember","Venus"]`.
- Media methods (`generate_image/video`, `create_music`, `create_duet`, `output_audio/video`) only log requests. They don't generate anything.

## v2 changes (docs/vala_reference/AnterranianEveCore_v2.vala)
- `EveBrainCell.lock_cell()`; `lock()` is kept as an alias.
- `store_memory` location defaults to `"Core"`.
- `npc_speak(dialogue, voice="Phoenix_Default_Voice", npc_name="NPC")` logs `"<npc_name> spoke"` @ `Game_World`, `Active`. `EveCore.npc_say(name, text, voice, npc_id)` routes to the NPC's companion core when `companions/<npc_id>/persona.json` exists, else the owner core. Wired: Welcome Island guide answers (MENU › Help) → owner core.

## Owner approval queue
`propose_update(desc)` logs a `PendingApproval` entry and adds it to `user://eve/proposals.json`. It stays pending until Phoenix taps Approve or Reject in **MENU › 📜 Proposals**. `EveCore.decide()` refuses anyone who isn't the owner.

## Wired hooks
- Chat: player lines (`AgentBrain.chat`) and companion replies (`reply_ready`, live or offline).
- Building: successful `spawn_structure`, `carve_area` and `place_voxel` tool calls (companion core), plus player Land Tools terraform (owner core).
- Music: every `MusicRadio.tune()` (owner core).

## BrainCore adapter
`EveCore.BrainAdapter` forwards every entry and proposal to a global `BrainCore` class when one exists, through `store_entry(id, entry)` and `queue_proposal(p)`. `feature/brain-core` was not on origin at port time, so local `user://eve` storage is the fallback and is always written. These two names are confirmed by the dev bot as the BrainCore API.

## Tests
`_eve_tests()` in `tests/run_tests.gd`: lock, owner unlock, plain hash, voice fallback, fire tag, duet, proposal gate, persistence.

# FAQ

Short answers. More detail is in the [Wiki](wiki/INDEX.md).

## Getting started

**How do I install it?**
Download the APK on your phone and tap it. Allow installs from that source if Android asks.

**How do I update?**
Install the new APK over the old one. Don't uninstall. Your stuff stays.

**Does it work offline?**
Yes. The world, avatar and offline companion replies all work. Live AI and SoundCloud need internet.

**Can I play in portrait?**
Yes. Portrait is the default. Landscape works too.

**How do I close the app?**
Tap **EXIT** under the minimap.

**How do I put it in the background?**
Tap **BG**, or press Android Back until it backgrounds.

**The tutorial island again?**
**MENU › Welcome Island**. You can skip it or go back anytime.

## Playing

**How do I move?**
Drag the left side to walk. Drag the right side to look.

**How do I fly?**
Tap **FLY**. Hold ▲ or ▼. Tap **LAND** to walk.

**How do I teleport?**
Open **◎ MAP** and tap a spot. Or use **MENU › 🧭 Teleport**.

**Why are there no names floating over people?**
They're off to cut clutter. Turn them on in Settings.

**Why can't I see region names on the map?**
They only show when you zoom in.

**Where can I fight?**
Only in the **Ember Arena** in Venus. Everywhere else is safe.

**How do I breed Wyrmlings?**
Feed two of them at the Wyrmling Nest, then breed the fed pair.

**Can I wear my own 3D items?**
Yes. Put a `.glb` in Download and tap **Import .glb wearable**.

## Companions

**Who are my companions?**
Foxy, Circuit Nova and Aaliyah walk with you by default.

**What voice does Foxy use?**
**Eve**. Canadian, raw, fiery.

**How do I talk to them?**
Tap **TALK** and type.

**Can I talk by voice?**
Not yet. Voice chat is **Planned**.

**Do companions keep living when the app is closed?**
Not yet. That needs the server (**Planned**).

**Can they learn?**
Yes. Teach them with "when I say X, reply Y". The owner approves what sticks.

## Owner (Phoenix)

**How do I unlock owner powers?**
**MENU › My Avatar & Profile**, enter your owner code and tap **Unlock**.

**Where do I approve what companions learned?**
**MENU › 📜 Proposals**. Tap Approve or Reject.

**Can I undo a change?**
Yes. Tap **Roll back** on a learned cell in Proposals.

**Where's a companion's memory?**
**MENU › 🕮 History**. Pick a companion and search.

**How do I back up a companion?**
In History, tap **Export**. Import merges it back.

**How do I change the land?**
**MENU › ⛰ Land Tools**: raise, lower, flatten, smooth, noise, revert.

**Can I set who enters my land?**
Yes, in the Region / Estate panel. It's enforced once the server exists.

**Is Aethel Coin real money?**
No. It's game-only for now. Cash-out and the exchange need legal review first.

## Worlds, places & money

**What worlds are there?**
Three realms: Alaskan Aurora Tundra, Venus Fire Wastes, Cosmic Glitter Expanse. See [Worlds & Regions](wiki/worlds-regions.md).

**Where are the popular places and events?**
**MENU › 🗺 Destinations** and its **📅 Events board**. See [Popular Places](wiki/popular-places.md).

**Can I trade Aethel Coin?**
Not yet. The exchange is partly built and needs legal review before going live. See [Aethel Coin Exchange](wiki/aethel-coin-exchange.md).

**How do I lock owner mode?**
Radial › **Security** › **Lock now**. See [Owner Lock](wiki/owner-lock.md).

## Troubleshooting

**The download stalls.**
Stay on Wi-Fi and keep the screen on. Delete the half file in Downloads, then try again.

**"App not installed" when I update.**
The new APK was signed with a different key than yours. Android blocks that. Use builds from the same source as your current one. If you must switch, back up first (History › Export), then uninstall and install.

**It says CHAT OFFLINE.**
Live chat needs an API key. Add it in **Settings › Companion AI** and set LIVE. Offline replies still work.

**No music plays.**
Check that **🔇** isn't on. Check your internet. Without a SoundCloud API key, songs open in the SoundCloud app instead.

**A parcel plays different music.**
That parcel has its own music URL. Leave it to hear the default.

**My .glb import failed.**
Newer Android can block reading Download. A file picker is **Planned**.

**The game is slow or hot.**
Tap **GFX** to drop to **LOW**.

**Proposals or History won't open for me.**
They're owner-only. Enter the owner code first.

**Where do I give feedback?**
Tell Foxy in chat. Gold **★ YOUR INPUT HERE** signs mark open decisions.
