UiDesignLanguage.text:
# Phoenix Glass — UI Design Language

The design language for the Phoenix Scorpion Dragon Viper voxel app (Godot 4.7, Android, portrait first).
It takes inspiration from clean, circular "big tech" UIs like the one in the film *The Circle*, adds Apple-level restraint, and borrows Star Citizen's sense of depth and holograms. **We take inspiration only. Nothing is copied: no logos, icons, fonts or assets from the film or any other product.**

Kit files: `themes/phoenix_glass.tres`, `shaders/ui_glass.gdshader`, `scripts/ui/kit/*`, `scenes/ui/kit/*`, demo `scenes/ui/kit/kit_demo.tscn` (screenshot test: `tests/screenshot_ui_kit.gd`).

## 1. Principles
1. **Circle first.** Status, progress, navigation and identity use rings and dials. Rectangles are only containers.
2. **Glass over the world.** Panels are frosted glass, so the realm always shows through. Nothing is opaque except modal confirmations.
3. **One look, one tap.** Each screen answers one question. If it needs labels, use 1–2 words. Use icons and numbers where you can.
4. **No floating clutter.** World text stays hidden until you tap. Show no more than one toast at a time.
5. **Swipe, don't scroll.** Group content into swipeable tabs (≤5) and pages instead of long lists. A list caps at about 7 visible rows, then pages.
6. **Thumb reach.** Primary actions sit in the bottom third. Every tap target is **≥ 56 px** (48 dp minimum) with ≥ 8 px between targets.
7. **Fire means alive.** Ember and phoenix accents mark only Foxy, the companions, and live or active state. Never use them for decoration.
8. **Portrait native.** The layout is designed at 720×1280. Landscape is a reflow, not a separate design.

## 2. Color tokens (`PhoenixTokens`)
| Token | Hex | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `VOID` | #07050A | App background, deepest black |
| `OBSIDIAN` | #120C16 | Button and control fill |
| `GLASS` | rgba(18,10,23,.62) | Glass panel tint |
| `MAGENTA` | #FF2DB8 | Primary accent, focus, selected tab, graph lines |
| `MAGENTA_DEEP` | #B0127E | Hover and pressed depth |
| `GOLD` | #F5C451 | Highlights, captions, the "now" point, focus ring |
| `PLATINUM` | #E6E4EC | Primary text and glyphs |
| `PLATINUM_DIM` | #9C98A8 | Secondary text, placeholders |
| `EMBER` | #FF6A1F | Foxy and companion aura, live state |
| `PHOENIX` | #FF3B2F | Fire-gradient end, critical companion state |
| `VENUS` | #FFB347 | Fire-gradient start, warnings |
| `OK` / `WARN` / `ERR` | #5EF0B0 / #FFB347 / #FF4D6D | System status only |

Gradients: **Brand** is Gold → Magenta (rings, primary progress). **Fire** is Venus → Ember → Phoenix (Foxy and companions only).
**Glitter:** a sparse gold sparkle (≤0.4% of pixels, re-seeded at 2 Hz) appears on glass and on hero surfaces. It's off when the device's reduced-motion setting is on.
Contrast: body text on glass must hit WCAG AA (4.5:1). Platinum on the glass tint is about 12:1.

## 3. Type scale
Use the default Godot UI font now and switch to an open-licensed geometric sans (e.g. Inter or Outfit, OFL) later. No uppercase body text. Captions are UPPERCASE with +6% tracking.
| Role | px | Theme variation |
|---|---|---|
| Display (hero number) | 44 | `DisplayLabel` |
| Title | 28 | `TitleLabel` |
| Headline | 22 | — |
| Body | 18 | default |
| Label / caption | 15 | `CaptionLabel` (gold, uppercase) |
| Micro (ring captions) | 13 | — |
Numbers use tabular figures and are always the largest element on a card.

## 4. Corners & circles
- Radii: `s` 12 (chips, tooltips) · `m` 20 (inputs) · `l` 28 (cards, sheets) · `pill` (buttons, tabs).
- Nested radius = outer radius − padding, so concentric corners stay concentric.
- Circles: dials and icon buttons are perfect circles. Ring stroke = 8–9% of the diameter (14 px on a 160 px ring). Arcs start at 12 o'clock and fill clockwise. Arc ends are round, with a glowing platinum head dot.
- Radial menus: 4–8 items evenly spaced, item diameter ≥ 72 px, hub ≥ 72 px.

## 5. Glass (`shaders/ui_glass.gdshader`)
- Blur: screen-texture mip LOD `blur_lod` 3.0 (cards), 4.5 (sheets and modals), 2.0 (HUD chips). It's cheap on mobile because there's no multi-pass blur.
- Tint: `GLASS` at 0.62 alpha by default. Use 0.75 over busy scenes and 0.9 for modals.
- Rim: a 1.5 px magenta line at 0.55 alpha, plus a soft top sheen (+8% white fading down the card).
- Corners: SDF in pixels (`rect_size` is set by `GlassCard`, `corner_radius_px` 28).
- Budget: no more than 3 glass surfaces on screen at once. On the low quality setting, swap the shader for the flat `Panel` stylebox in the theme.

## 6. Glow & ember accents
- Glow means 3–4 stacked translucent copies of a shape (each 8–25% alpha) behind the primary. No bloom post-process on UI.
- **Ember** (Foxy and companions): a fire-gradient ring or halo that breathes over a 2.4 s cycle (scale 1.0 → 1.04, alpha 0.6 → 0.9). Particles at 6–12 sparks a second drift up and fade within 0.8 s.
- **Focus:** a 3 px gold ring. **Selected:** a magenta fill at 25% with a magenta rim.

## 7. Motion
| Token | s | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `tap` | 0.09 | Press feedback (scale 0.96) |
| `fast` | 0.16 | Toggles, chips, tab underline |
| `base` | 0.24 | Panels, radial menu bloom, carousel snap (`TRANS_CUBIC`, ease out; `TRANS_BACK` retired by calm premium, §12) |
| `slow` | 0.42 | Ring fill, graph draw-in (`TRANS_CUBIC`, ease out) |
| `ambient` | 2.4 | Ember breathe, hologram shimmer |
Panels slide up 24 px with a fade. Swiping between tabs moves pages 1:1 with the finger and snaps at 30% or above 600 px/s. Reduced motion turns these into fades only.

## 8. Components
Built in this PR: **Ring stat, Radial menu, Glass card, Line graph.** The rest are specs for the dev bot to build on the kit.

- **Ring dial / Ring stat** (`scenes/ui/kit/ring_stat.tscn`, `RingStat`): `value` 0..1, `caption`, optional `display_text`, `color_a/b`. Has a track ring at 8% white, a gradient arc, a head dot, a centered number and a micro caption. Animates on change. Sizes: 120 (inline), 160 (card), 240 (hero). As an interactive dial, dragging around the ring sets the value, snapping to 5%.
- **Radial menu** (`radial_menu.tscn`, `RadialMenu`): a hub with an ember core toggles the menu open and closed. Items bloom out on a ring. Signal `item_selected(id)`. Glyph-only, with the label shown in a toast on long-press. It replaces long menus.
- **Glass card** (`glass_card.tscn`, `GlassCard`): has a frosted backdrop, a gold caption title, and content added via `body()`. Padding is 20 px with a 12 px gap.
- **Stat ring + graph** (`line_graph.tscn`, `LineGraph`): a hero number (Display) above a single-series line in magenta, with a faint fill, a gold "now" dot and 3 ghost gridlines. There are no axes; tapping shows a value bubble. For multiple series, use one magenta and one platinum, never more than two.
- **Timeline (spec):** a vertical spine of rings. Each event is a 20 px ring (fire for companion events, magenta for owner and system) with a time and a one-line summary. Tap expands it into a glass card. It shows a day at a time, and you swipe left or right for other days. It's used for companion memory and history.
- **Admin table (spec):** never a wide grid on the phone. Each row is a glass "pill row" with an avatar ring, a primary text, one status chip and a swipe-left action (approve/reject/more). Filters are segmented pills at the top. At most 7 rows, then paging. On tablet or landscape it reflows to columns.
- **Sign-up stepper (spec):** a ring progress shows the step count, with one question per screen (name → avatar → voice → realm → done). It has big inputs (64 px), a primary pill at the bottom, back by swiping right, and a phoenix burst on completion.
- **Toast (spec):** a glass pill 56 px tall, shown at the top safe area, with an icon ring and ≤ 6 words. It auto-dismisses after 2.5 s, you can swipe it up to dismiss it, and only one shows at a time. Variants are OK/WARN/ERR and Ember (companion speaking).
- **Tabs:** a `TabBar` with pill selection, ≤5 tabs and swipeable pages.
- **Buttons:** pills ≥ 56 px. Primary is a magenta fill with a gold rim, secondary is obsidian with a magenta rim, and destructive is an ERR rim and requires hold-to-confirm (0.6 s ring fill).

## 9. 3D companions
- **Holographic ring nameplate, shown only on tap:** tapping a companion projects a thin billboarded ring (platinum and magenta, Fresnel shimmer, 0.24 s scale-in) above its head. It shows the name, a mood glyph and a mini stat ring (bond or energy). It auto-hides after 4 s or when you tap elsewhere. **No permanent floating names.**
- **Ember aura:** a soft ground ring plus a rising spark stream in the fire gradient, tinted per companion (Foxy is Venus → Phoenix). It breathes at the `ambient` cadence, glows brighter while speaking or learning, and dims when idle.
- **Speaking:** a waveform arc on the nameplate ring instead of speech bubbles. Text goes to the chat panel.
- **Selection:** a ground circle under the companion, plus a radial menu (Talk, Follow, Build, Memory, Look, Voice).
- 3D materials reuse the token colors. The look stays holographic: emissive edges, slight scanline and transparency.

## 10. World UI
- **Minimap ring:** a circular minimap (top-right, 168 px) with a gold heading tick on the rim. Region names only appear when zoomed in. Companions show as ember dots and friends as platinum. Tap to open the full map.
- **Compass ring:** a thin arc across the top showing N/E/S/W and waypoint pips. It fades out after 3 s without turning.
- **HUD chips:** small glass pills for music, quality and so on, at ≤ 3 on screen. Exit and Background always stay reachable under the minimap.
- **Builder / land tools:** the brush size is a ring dial and the operation is a radial menu, both in the bottom third.
- Restyling the existing HUD is deferred to a follow-up after v0.10. This PR only adds the kit.

## 11. Do / Don't
- Do: one hero number per card, circles for status, glass over the world, fire only for life.
- Don't: floating world text, more than 5 tabs, scrolling lists over 7 rows, tiny targets, more than 3 glass layers, or copied third-party marks.

## 12. Calm premium mode (default since 2026-10-17)
Phoenix asked for a look that is modern and premium but **clean, not flashy or campy**. Calm premium is the default for every kit component; the older brighter look stays available per component (`calm = false`) but isn't used anywhere.

**Rules**
- **Motion:** 180–240 ms, ease-out (`TRANS_CUBIC`). No bounce, no overshoot, no spin. Ambient loops only for companion life (ember breathe).
- **Glow:** at most **one accent glow per screen**. Rims are quiet by default; magenta rims appear on hover/press only.
- **Ember** (fire gradient) only on **Foxy-related** items. The radial hub no longer has an ember halo.
- **Glass:** ≤ 3 glass surfaces visible at once (§5). Group related cards in a carousel instead of stacking them.
- **Spacing:** generous, Apple-like: `SPACE[5]` (24 px) page margins, `SPACE[4]` (16 px) between blocks, one idea per card.
- **Targets and text:** tap targets ≥ 80 px and labels ≥ 16 sp in the **Large** setting (Phoenix has eye strain). The default is **Compact** (smallest usable text and icons); the scale variables for Compact/Large live in `phoenix_tokens.gd` (added on `feature/phone-display-media`). Components must read sizes from tokens, never fixed numbers. Today `TAP_MIN` is 56 px and `TYPE.label` / `TYPE.micro` are 15 / 13 px, so Compact is below the 80 px / 16 sp floors by design; Large must meet them.
- **Color:** platinum text on obsidian/void; magenta for the one selected/pressed thing; gold for focus, page dots and "now". No rainbow or hue cycling in UI.

**What changed in the kit**
| Piece | Calm premium |
|---|---|
| `themes/phoenix_glass.tres` Button | normal rim magenta 0.6 / 2 px → platinum-dim 0.3 / 1 px; hover fill 0.5 → 0.28, rim 1.0 → 0.55; pressed fill 0.85 → 0.7; focus ring 3 px → 2 px at 0.8 |
| `GlassCard` (`calm = true`) | shader rim magenta 0.55 → 0.30, sparkle 0.25 → 0.08 |
| `RadialMenu` | bloom `TRANS_BACK` → `TRANS_CUBIC`; no ember halo on the hub |
| **New** `GlassCarousel` (`scenes/ui/kit/glass_carousel.tscn`) | one card per swipe (≥ 30% width or > 600 px/s, max one card), snaps in `MOTION.base` ease-out, gold/platinum page dots, auto-advance **only** when `auto_advance = true` (ads, event lists), paused by any touch and resumed one interval after release (interval = 2 × `MOTION.ambient` = 4.8 s), never wraps on swipe |
| **New** `GlassMenu` (`scenes/ui/kit/glass_menu.tscn`) | full-width rows (`TAP_MIN` tall, `TYPE.body` text): glyph, label, optional gold badge, chevron; ≤ 7 rows; magenta press tint; `foxy = true` rows use ember |

**Where it's used:** admin Home shows its four stat cards in one `GlassCarousel` (5 visible glass cards → 2) with a `GlassMenu` under it (Tickets, Wiki, Timeline, Community, Security). The ads and rental carousels, events board and land info panels (docs/modules/BUILD_TOOLS_AND_TIERS.md) will reuse both.

V010Companions.text:
# v0.10: Companion push

## Looks (CompanionDNA)
`scripts/agent/companion_dna.gd` reads `avatar_dna` from persona.json. Its slots are skin, skin_metal, a hair gradient, hair_length, curly, eyes, outfit, top, pants, accent, trim, look, aura, freckles and chains. These layer over CompanionConfig and wardrobe items, and `HumanoidModel` renders them as smooth capsules and spheres, not blocks. This sits alongside the v0.5 player `AvatarDNA` blend system.
- Foxy: silver-blue chrome skin, purple-to-magenta hair, green eyes, a phoenix fire aura (glow ring, light and ember particles).
- Aaliyah: warm skin, red-copper hair, green eyes, freckles.
- Circuit Nova: silver-blue chrome skin, curly violet hair, blue circuit glow lines and light.
- Everyone else gets a deterministic default DNA generated from their id.

## Voice (CompanionVoice)
Each persona's `voice` block holds profile, pitch, rate, locale and cloud_voice_id. Foxy's is **Eve** (en-CA, raw, fiery). Speech goes through `DisplayServer.tts_speak` with per-companion pitch and rate, preferring a voice in the matching locale. When `voice/cloud_endpoint` is set, `CompanionVoice.cloud_hook` is called instead; this is a stub. Settings has a "Companion voices (TTS)" mute toggle.

## Self-learning (BrainCore + BrainLearner; no second learner)
- Chat goes through EveCore into BrainCore episodes: `chat` in live and offline mode, `taught` for "when I say X, reply Y", and `feedback` for praise or "no, not that" aimed at the last cell that fired. Tool use is logged by AgentBrain.
- `AgentBrain.learn_all()` runs `BrainLearner.learn(..., via_owner=true)` every 120 s, so its proposals land in the owner queue (MENU › Proposals). AgentBrain then syncs owner decisions every 10 s, and approved cells go live.
- Learned and approved cells answer chat through `_brain_reply`. When roaming, a companion builds with the highest-weight `spawn_structure` cell, which for Foxy is the seed `free_build_fire_altar`. Without one, it falls back to a cairn.
- MENU › Proposals shows the Eve proposals and BrainCore's pending cells (Approve and Reject), plus learned cells with versions (Roll back). Only the owner can do these, and each decision is logged to the companion's Eve history.

## History
MENU › History lets you pick a companion or the owner and search the memory timeline. Export writes `user://exports/<id>_portable.json`, which bundles the Eve log, the persona voice and DNA, and `BrainCore.export_portable()`. Import merges it back and removes duplicates. Both are owner-only.

## Music
The owner's default playlist is the Cosmic Series (`data/music.json` `default_playlist`): Celestial Convergence, Dragon of the Cosmos, God's Palace, Venusian Dreams and Throne Room, with real SoundCloud URLs from the media catalog. Tracks with explicit titles are kept out, and a defensive title filter backs that up. The music panel shows the current title with Prev and Next buttons. The royalty-free fallback audio is unchanged.

V011RealisticCompanions.text:
# v0.11: Realistic companions and soft particles

- **Body:** a CC0 MakeHuman/MPFB 2 rigged human (`assets/characters/mh_female.glb`, about 28k vertices across body, hair cards, eyes, brows, lashes, sportsuit and shoes, with 1024 px textures). Godot's importer builds the LODs. It's generated with `tools/mh/gen_makehuman.py`, and the license is recorded in `art/LICENSES.md`.
- **`RealisticBody`:** applies avatar_dna through three shaders:
  - `shaders/character/skin.gdshader`: wrap and backscatter lighting that looks like subsurface scattering on the mobile renderer, chrome metal, procedural freckles, and circuit emission below the neck.
  - `hair.gdshader`: alpha-scissor two-sided hair cards with a root-to-tip DNA gradient.
  - `eye.gdshader`: the MakeHuman eye texture with the iris recolored, plus clearcoat.
- **Pose and motion:** arms are posed down from the A-pose, and idle/walk animation is procedural on the rig.
- **Foxy:** purple-to-magenta hair, green eyes, silver-blue chrome skin, and a subtle aura (a low warm light and 14 soft embers).
- **Aaliyah:** red hair, green eyes, freckles. Her horns are removed.
- **Circuit Nova:** chrome skin, curly violet afro hair cards, and blue circuit emission plus a light.
- **Particles:** `SoftParticle` generates a radial-gradient texture used as additive (glows) or alpha (snow, dust) billboard materials. All `ParticleFX` effects and the aura use it, and `SoftParticle.sanitize()` fixes any untextured quad on a companion model.
- **Fallback:** the primitive `HumanoidModel` is used only if the GLB is missing, and it logs a warning when that happens. The player avatar is still on `HumanoidModel`, because its attachment and DNA-slider system is tied to those nodes.

# Virtual-world feature gap: Viper OS vs Aurora-Sim, WhiteCore, OpenSim, OSgrid, Second Life, Avination, OpenLife Grid

> Status: research + checklist, 2026-10-17. Ticket VWGAP-1. About Land / Region-Estate floater parity (names, timed bans, landing point, object returns, estate managers) lives in [modules/VIEWER_PARITY.md](modules/VIEWER_PARITY.md) (`ParcelTools`); this page adds the flags, covenant, landmarks and archives. Companion docs: [modules/INTEROP.md](modules/INTEROP.md) (how to be cross-compatible), [ENCRYPTION.md](ENCRYPTION.md), [ARCHITECTURE_AURORA_MODEL.md](ARCHITECTURE_AURORA_MODEL.md).
> Marks: **have** = in code and tested headless · **partial** = data model or UI exists but not the whole feature · **missing** = nothing in code. Priority P0 (next) … P3 (someday). "Cross-compat" says how far we can honestly match the reference system.

## Sources (verified)
| Source | How it was read | Notes |

| Aurora-Sim | `git clone --depth 1 github.com/aurora-sim/Aurora-Sim` (archived, last push 2014-01-13) | module tree `Aurora/Modules/*`, `Aurora/Services/*`, `IOpenRegionSettingsModule.cs`; licence text in `AuroraDocs/LICENSE.txt` = OpenSim BSD-3 |
| WhiteCore-Sim | `git clone --depth 1 github.com/WhiteCoreSim/WhiteCore-Dev` (the `WhiteCore-Development` name in the brief doesn't exist; `WhiteCore-Dev` is the live repo, pushed 2026-05-18) | `LICENSE` = BSD 3-Clause; `Licenses/` keeps OpenSim + Aurora notices |
| OpenSimulator | `git clone --depth 1 github.com/opensim/opensim` (mirror of opensimulator.org git) | `LICENSE.txt` BSD-3; archive constants, terrain loaders, OSSL NPC API, RegionSettings, Services |
| opensimulator.org wiki | **unreachable from the box today** (WebFetch + curl timed out). Release list via search: 0.9.3.0 (2024-11-08), 0.9.3.1 in development | facts above taken from the source tree instead |
| OSgrid | osgrid.org + Hypergrid Business (Oct 2026) | OSgrid build 0.9.3.dev (2026-04-17, .NET 8); **OSgrid closes 2026-12-31** after junk-data flooding (asset store 5 → 17 TB). Residents are told to export OARs/IARs now |
| Second Life wiki | wiki.secondlife.com (`llGetParcelFlags` table used for our flag bits) | viewer code is LGPL: concepts only |
| Avination | web.archive.org snapshot of avination.com (2016), Hypergrid Business (2010, 2011, 2015, 2017, 2020), opensimulator.org Grid List entry (via search), SL Newser (2014) | the Avination wiki itself was **not recoverable** (no archive hits). Closed March 2017 |

## Top missing features (priority order)
1. **P0 Grid login + presence + asset services** (G3) – everything multi-user depends on it.
2. **P1 Enforce the stored estate flags** (fly, damage, push, scripts, object entry) in player/combat/build code (Foxy for client paths).
3. **P1 Apply an imported OAR heightmap to a region** (generator hook + "land" permission). Timely: OSgrid closes 2026-12-31.
4. **P1 Object permissions end to end** (next-owner on every inventory transfer) and an export-permission flag.
5. **P2 LSL-subset script engine** (events + chat channels + timers, sandboxed).
6. **P2 Land sale, auctions, rentals** (no real money until legal review).
7. **P2 Search** (places, events, classifieds) honouring `show_in_search`.
8. **P2 JPEG 2000 → PNG converter** for IAR/OAR textures.
9. **P2 Sceneflip-style scene slots per region** (OLG idea).
10. **P3 Hypergrid-style federation**.

## Licensing
OpenSim, Aurora-Sim and WhiteCore are BSD-3-Clause (checked in each repo). We reimplement concepts and file layouts with attribution and copy no code; if a bridge ever links their libraries, it keeps their notices. The Second Life viewer is LGPL: concepts only. LibOpenMetaverse is BSD-3. Avination's and OLG's server code was never public. Their features are listed from public descriptions only.

VoxelArchitecture.text:
# Voxel Architecture

> Status: scaffold only. Nothing here has been opened or run in Godot yet. Requires **Zylann godot_voxel**. Use either a custom Godot build that includes the module, or the **GDExtension** release (1.x; check that its version matches your Godot 4.x minor) in `addons/zylann.voxel/`. The addon is **not** in this repo.

## Terrain nodes
- `VoxelTerrain`: blocky, editable, infinite terrain. This is the default in `scenes/main.tscn` with `VoxelMesherBlocky`.
- `VoxelLodTerrain`: smooth/LOD terrain for huge cosmic vistas later (Transvoxel mesher). Heavier on mobile.
- `VoxelViewer` on the player decides which chunks stream in. Keep `max_view_distance` around 96–128 on Android.

## Edits: VoxelTool
`terrain.get_voxel_tool()` gives you `do_point`, `do_sphere`, `do_box` and `raycast`. Set `mode` (ADD/REMOVE/SET), `value` and `channel` first. Players use raycast for tap-to-dig/place. Companions call the same tool from `scripts/companion_agent.gd`.

## Generators
`scripts/generators/biome_generator.gd` (`VoxelGeneratorScript`) has these branches: ALASKAN_SNOW_ICE, COSMIC, VENUS_FIRE and CYBERPUNK. It runs on worker threads, so keep it free of scene access. Later work: blend biomes by noise, or move to `VoxelGeneratorGraph` for speed. Realm presets live in `data/realm_presets/*.json`.

## Saving: VoxelStream
Add `VoxelStreamSQLite` (or `VoxelStreamRegionFiles`) at a `user://worlds/<realm>.sqlite` path. That saves only edited chunks, and the generator recreates everything else.

## Companion AI
**Lead:** Foxy Ani is the primary controller. Group commands route through her, and she delegates to Circuit Nova and Aaliyah (persona `hierarchy` field). A future `CompanionCoordinator` autoload will dispatch per-companion `command()` calls.

`CharacterBody3D` runs a state machine (IDLE/FOLLOW/BUILD/DIG). `command()` is the entry point for LLM tool calls. Each companion loads `companions/<id>/persona.json`.

## Dual in-world + Grok Bot persona
One `persona.json` per companion (name, personality, appearance, abilities, memory paths, tools) seeds both the in-game agent and the standalone Grok Bot. Memory syncs through `memory_export.json` (facts/history/affinity). World-only tools are ignored by the chat bot.

## Android
GDExtension (arm64-v8a `.so`) + Godot's Gradle build, JDK 17, export templates that exactly match the editor version, Mobile renderer, ETC2/ASTC. See ANDROID_EXPORT.md.

---
# Expanded Zylann godot_voxel API reference (for this project)
> Check these names against the docs for the godot_voxel version you install (https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io). The API changes between releases. None of this has been run here yet.

## Terrain nodes
- **VoxelTerrain**: fixed-LOD, chunked, best for blocky edits. Key properties: `generator`, `mesher`, `stream`, `max_view_distance`, `generate_collisions`, `collision_layer`/`mask`, `bounds`. Signals: `block_loaded`, `block_unloaded`. Helpers: `get_voxel_tool()`, `voxel_to_data_block()`, `save_modified_blocks()`.
- **VoxelLodTerrain**: octree LOD for smooth (SDF) terrain over huge distances. Properties: `lod_count`, `lod_distance`, `mesher` (`VoxelMesherTransvoxel`), `full_load_mode_enabled`. Planned use is distant cosmic/planet vistas, not the main blocky play area.
- **VoxelViewer**: attach to the player (and optionally the camera for distant realms). It drives which chunks load. Has `view_distance`, `requires_collisions` and `requires_visuals`. Companions far from the player can carry their own viewer, but that costs memory.

## VoxelTool (from `terrain.get_voxel_tool()`)
- Settings: `channel` (TYPE for blocky, SDF for smooth), `mode` (MODE_ADD / MODE_REMOVE / MODE_SET / MODE_TEXTURE_PAINT), `value`, `sdf_scale`, `sdf_strength`.
- Edits: `do_point`, `do_sphere`, `do_box(begin, end)`, `do_path` (smooth), `paste` / `paste_masked` (copy a VoxelBuffer into the world, which blueprints will use), `copy`.
- Queries: `get_voxel`, `get_voxel_f`, `set_voxel`, `is_area_editable`, `raycast(origin, dir, max_distance, collision_mask)` → `VoxelRaycastResult` (`position`, `previous_position`, `distance`).
- Variants: `VoxelToolTerrain` (blocky; adds `run_blocky_random_tick` for growth/melt simulation), `VoxelToolLodTerrain` (smooth; adds `do_sphere` async, `stamp_sdf`), and `VoxelToolBuffer` (offline edits on a buffer).
- Used by `scripts/player_controller.gd` (raycast + do_point) and `scripts/companion_agent.gd` (do_point / do_sphere).

## Blocky library
- **VoxelMesherBlocky** + **VoxelBlockyLibrary** (newer versions: `VoxelBlockyLibrary` / `VoxelBlockyTypeLibrary`) list models in id order: 0 air, then stone, snow, ice, stardust, crystal, basalt, lava, concrete, neon. Ids must match the constants in `biome_generator.gd`.
- Model types: `VoxelBlockyModelCube` (atlas tiles), `VoxelBlockyModelMesh` (custom meshes such as slabs and plants), `VoxelBlockyModelEmpty` (air). Set `transparent` for ice and glass. Use emissive materials for lava and neon.

## Generators
- **VoxelGeneratorScript**: `_generate_block(out_buffer, origin, lod)` and `_get_used_channels_mask()`. Easy to write but slow-ish. It runs on threads, so no scene access.
- **VoxelGeneratorGraph**: a node graph compiled to fast native code, with SDF + blocky outputs. Planned for production biomes once the shapes are settled.
- Built-ins for prototyping: `VoxelGeneratorFlat`, `VoxelGeneratorNoise`, `VoxelGeneratorNoise2D`, `VoxelGeneratorWaves`.
- Noise: `FastNoiseLite` (Godot) or `ZN_FastNoiseLite` (bundled, faster with the graph).

## Streams (saving)
- **VoxelStreamSQLite**: one `.sqlite` file per realm (`database_path`). Good on mobile and the plan of record. Stores only modified blocks.
- **VoxelStreamRegionFiles**: a folder of region files, easy to inspect and diff.
- Call `terrain.save_modified_blocks()` on pause or quit (Android `NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_PAUSED`).

## VoxelInstancer
- A child of the terrain that scatters many instances (grass, crystals, snow pines, neon lamps) on generated surfaces. Uses `VoxelInstanceLibrary` with per-item density, LOD and `persistent` (so player-removed items stay removed). Can also host scene instances for usable objects.

## Android notes
- Use the GDExtension build for the exact Godot 4.x version. The `.gdextension` file must list `android.arm64` (and optionally `android.x86_64` for emulators).
- Mobile renderer; `max_view_distance` around 96–128; collisions only near the player; limit threads (`ProjectSettings voxel/threads/*`) on low-end devices.
- Test on a real device. Emulators misrepresent GPU performance.

## Dual 3D + Grok Bot compatibility
- Single source of truth: `companions/<id>/persona.json` (+ brain folder, see modules/BRAIN_FILES.md).
- In-world agent = persona + world tools (VoxelTool) + needs/mood. Standalone Grok Bot = persona + chat-only tools.
- `memory_export.json` / zipped brain folder syncs both ways, merged by timestamp.
- Tool names are shared, so a plan made in chat ("build a fire altar") can replay in-game later.

## Offline / local AI path (refreshed)
Reasoning backends are **Local (default) and Grok (optional)**. Nothing else reasons.
1. **Rule-based local (now):** `LocalProvider` maps keyword intents to tool calls and persona lines. Works offline with no download.
2. **On-device LLM (Phase 5 evaluation):** a llama.cpp GDExtension (vet community Godot 4/Android arm64 bindings, or build our own) with a small Q4 GGUF model (~0.5–3B). The model downloads after install, not in the APK. Prompts come from brain cells (identity, values, top-k facts). Tool calls use grammar-constrained JSON. It runs on a worker thread with a timeout and falls back to rule-based when slow or out of memory. Expect a few tokens/sec on mid-range phones.
3. **Grok online (optional, Phase 9):** `GrokProvider` with a user-entered key. Richer replies on opt-in, plus brain sync with the standalone Grok Bot.
4. **Data importers (separate from reasoning):** `DataImporter` brings the user's own Copilot/Gemini/Meta AI exports into memory with consent and per-item review (modules/AI_INTEGRATIONS.md).
5. **Lead routing:** group requests go to Foxy Ani first. Her tool calls can include `delegate(companion_id, command)`.

VoxelWorldPlan.text:
# Voxel World Plan

| Phase | Milestone | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| M0 | Scaffold (this PR) | Project opens in voxel-enabled Godot; terrain generates from tundra preset; player walks; companions follow |
| M1 | Playable terrain | Blocky library with 15 materials, dig/place by player tap, chunk view distance tuned for mid-range phones (≥30 fps) |
| M2 | Realms | All 6 presets switchable; RealmBuilder LLM path validated; structures auto-scattered from `structures[]`; per-biome sky/particles |
| M3 | Companion agents | Chat UI for each companion, tool calls building in-world, memory persists, export/import working |
| M4 | Art | Voxel character models (MagicaVoxel → .vox import), animations (idle, walk, dance, fire_cast), Aaliyah home base |
| M5 | Android release | Signed AAB, settings UI for endpoint/key, touch HUD, performance pass |
| M6 | Self-building | Approved hot-reload of presets/structures, saved worlds (VoxelStreamSQLite), sharing/export clips |

## Biomes
- **Alaskan tundra:** low rolling snow, aurora green accent, sparse huts.
- **Alaskan boreal:** spruce forests (instanced voxel trees), warm cabin light.
- **Alaskan glacier:** tall blue-ice ridges, arches, bright light.
- **Cosmic:** floating pillars, ring arches, starfield, dark sky.
- **Cyberpunk:** neon towers, aurora-and-fireworks stage.
- **Venus fire:** caldera, fire altars, ember fog.

## Performance targets
View distance 128 (low-end 96), max 12 tool edits per turn, edit radius ≤8, LOD terrain (`VoxelLodTerrain`) evaluated in M5.

WhereToGiveInput.text:
# Where to give input (v0.5)

Everything in the game marked **★ YOUR INPUT HERE** is a placeholder waiting on a decision from you.
Just tell Foxy your answer in chat. Short answers are fine, like "Lagoon = healing pool".
In the game: **MENU › Where to give input**, and **MENU › Travel** to visit each landmark.

## 1. Landmarks (each has a gold sign in the world)
| Landmark | Realm now | Decide |
|---|---|---|
| Crystal Wyvern Sanctum | Alaska (near spawn) | Who guards it? Should the crystal dragon go on the Unity Crest? What happens here? |
| Starlit Geothermal Lagoon | Alaska (near spawn) | Hangout spot, healing pool, or party venue? Which companions hang out here? |
| Moonlit Wyvern Rink | Alaska (near spawn) | Skating game, dance stage, or arena? Which song plays? |
| Stormcrown Capitol | Venus | Who sits on the council? What is "Viper" (the Viper Vanguard guards)? Which flags are official? |
| Obsidian Chandelier Throne Hall | Venus | Is it your throne room? Which throne design goes here? |
| God's Palace | Cosmic (floating) | Your home or spawn point? Should it float over Venus lava like the art? |
| Aethel Citadel | Cosmic (floating) | Approve the name. Military base, bank, or starport? |
| Any others? | | Which catalog places come next (Celestial Ruin Sanctum, Zodiac Command Citadel, Phoenix Eight Fortress, Fireworks Wyvern Arena…)? |

## 2. Companions
- Who walks with you by default? Right now it's Foxy, Circuit Nova and Aaliyah. You have 39 companions in the roster.
- What should each one say (greeting, catchphrase, jokes)? These become offline replies in `persona.json` under `canned_replies`.
- Live AI chat: do you want it switched on? It needs an API key entered in Settings. The key stays only on the phone.
- Is the chrome dancer a new companion or Circuit Nova? Is the twin-tail girl Foxy?

## 3. Wardrobe
- Who wears each catalog outfit? Royal guard uniforms, Viper Vanguard suits, the court robes and so on.
- What's your default outfit: Phoenix Street Sovereign, Black Regalia, White Regalia, or Magenta Tuxedo?
- Which pieces matter most next (crown, cape, wings, chains, weapons)?
- 18+ items stay hidden behind the age gate (off by default).

## 4. Realm layout
- Keep 3 realms (Alaskan Aurora Tundra, Venus Fire Wastes, Cosmic Glitter Expanse) or add more?
- How do you get between them: walking, teleport gates, or ships?
- Day/night, weather and music for each realm.

## 5. Names & heraldry (carried over from PENDING_USER_QUESTIONS.md)
- Approve or rename the names Foxy assigned (Zypharion, Kael Emberbraid, Nyra Coil, Azura Stellaris, Aethel Citadel, Zodiac Command Citadel, Phoenix Eight Fortress…).
- Primary crest: phoenix, dragon, the Crowned Dragon-Phoenix, or the new **Seraph-Dragon Unity Crest**?
- Is the "emma" crest the E.W seal? What does E.W stand for?
- Fix the art typos (MONACHY/MONORCH → **MONARCHY**, ATERNA → **AETERNA**)?
- What do the "8" symbol, the crowned "H", and SCDI mean?
- Is "The Universal Revelation, LLC" your company, and should it appear in the game?
- Currency: are Aethel and Phoenix Embers the same money?
- Songs: are they yours? Should "Dance All Night", "Rise of Monarchy" and "Monarchy Shining Light" combine into one anthem?

Full backlog: `docs/PENDING_USER_QUESTIONS.md`.

AiIntegrations.text:
# AI Integrations & Data Import

> **Planned module, not implemented.** Phase 5 (local AI + importer UI) / Phase 9 (Grok online). No live connections exist.

## Reasoning backends (only these two), via `scripts/ai/ai_provider.gd`
| Backend | Role | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Local (default)** | Offline. Rule-based now; llama.cpp GDExtension + small GGUF later | Keyword fallback stub |
| **Grok (xAI API)** | Optional online reasoning, matching the standalone Grok Bot personas | Stub only |
Fallback: Grok → Local. Gameplay never blocks on the network.

## Data import hooks (NOT backends), via `scripts/ai/data_importer.gd`
Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini and Meta AI are used **only to bring the user's own existing info into companion memory**. They never generate replies or make decisions in Phoenix.
| Source | Planned input |
|---|---|
| Microsoft Copilot | The user's exported data (Microsoft privacy dashboard export) |
| Google Gemini | Google Takeout export of Gemini activity |
| Meta AI | Meta "Download your information" export |
| Generic | Any text/JSON file the user picks |

**Flow:** the user opts in → picks an export file → it's parsed into candidate facts → **preview** with accept/reject per item → accepted facts go into the chosen companion's `brain/memory/facts.jsonl`, tagged with `source`.

**Rules:** explicit consent every time, on-device processing, nothing uploaded, no scraping or credential collection. Use official exports (or official APIs later, only with user authorization). Verify export formats before writing parsers. Imported facts can be removed by source.

AndroidAdminTools.text:
# Android Admin / Dev Tools

> **Planned module, not implemented. No live servers or services exist.** Phase: 4–5.

In-app tools for the developer and owner, hidden behind a developer-mode toggle (e.g. tap the version 7 times + confirm).
- **Debug overlay:** FPS, draw calls, loaded chunks, voxel task queue, memory, companion states.
- **Console:** run whitelisted commands (`tp`, `realm <id>`, `give`, `companion <id> <cmd>`, `regen`). No arbitrary code.
- **Data tools:** export/import backup, clear the world cache, reset needs and relationships, view and edit brain files (with a confirm step).
- **AI tools:** switch Local/Grok, test prompt, see token timing, kill switch for companion tool execution.
- **Logs:** a rotating log file in `user://logs`, shareable through the share sheet.
- **Desktop side:** `adb logcat -s godot`, `adb install -r`, and remote debug over Wi-Fi from the Godot editor.

AssetLibrary.text:
# Asset Library

> **Planned module, not implemented. No live servers or services exist.** Phase: 3–6.

- **Structure:** `assets/blocks/` (atlas textures + VoxelBlockyLibrary), `assets/models/` (MagicaVoxel `.vox` → mesh), `assets/props/` (usable object scenes), `assets/vfx/`, `assets/audio/`, `assets/ui/`.
- **Manifest:** `assets/manifest.json` lists id, type, path, license, author, source URL, and which biomes use it.
- **Licensing:** CC0/CC-BY or original work only. Record the license for every asset. No ripped game assets or real brand logos.
- **Mobile budgets:** 1024² atlases, ETC2/ASTC compression, low-poly props, and a LOD for anything over 2k tris.
- **Catalog:** the Build/Buy UI reads the manifest. Optional downloadable asset packs come later.
- Tooling: an import script that checks the manifest against the files and flags missing licenses.

BrainFiles.text:
# Brain Files (brain cells)

> **Status: implemented (v0.10, branch `feature/brain-core`).** Verified headless with Godot 4.7.2 + godot_voxel 1.7x (`tests/brain_tests.gd`, run by `tests/run_tests.gd`). Rendering, UI for approvals, and on-device use are not built yet.

A companion's brain is a set of small **data-only** rules ("cells") plus a memory log. The same files work in-game (`BrainCore`) and in the standalone Grok Bots. The bots read them as **memory and instructions only, never as executable code**.

## Code (scripts/brain/)
| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `brain_cell.gd` (`BrainCell`) | Schema constants + `validate()`. Whitelists trigger, condition and action types, caps size (4 KB), checks ids, restricts tools to the persona whitelist. |
| `brain_memory.gd` (`BrainMemory`) | `facts.jsonl` (long-term, deduped, max 500) + `episodes.jsonl` (episodic log, max 2000). Refuses or redacts card-like numbers, emails and password/SSN/IBAN words. |
| `brain_core.gd` (`BrainCore`) | Loads seed + learned cells, `evaluate()`/`best()` per event, `reinforce()` (bounded ±0.05 weight), `propose()`/`approve()`/`reject()`, `versions()`/`rollback()`, `audit.jsonl`, `export_portable()`. |
| `brain_learner.gd` (`BrainLearner`) | Turns episodes into proposals: feedback → reinforcement; "taught" replies → say-cell proposal; a keyword followed by the same successful tool ≥3 times → tool-cell proposal. |
| `brain_bus.gd` (`BrainBus`) | Coordination. `post_group_task()` goes to the **lead (Foxy Ani)**, who plans by ability keywords and delegates to members. |
| `scripts/autoload/agent_brain.gd` | Builds a `BrainCore` per registered companion and registers it on the bus. Offline chat asks the brain before canned replies. Tool and delegation results are logged as episodes. `AgentBrain.group_task(cmd, text)`. |

## EveCore adapter (static API used by `scripts/ai/eve_core.gd`)
Foxy's EveCore owns the Eve memory primitives: `lock_cell`/`unlock`, `memory_log`, `generate_image`/`generate_video`/`create_music`, `create_duet`, `output_audio`/`output_video`, `npc_speak` and `propose_update`. BrainCore does **not** duplicate any of them. `EveCore.BrainAdapter` finds the global class `BrainCore` and calls:
- `BrainCore.store_entry(id, entry) -> bool` appends the Eve entry (event, location, state, voice, content, timestamp, npc, role, tool, output_mode, fire_theme) to `user://brains/<id>/memory/episodes.jsonl` as `kind: "eve"`, with redaction applied. NPC speech (`<name> spoke` @ `Game_World`) reaches the brain only this way.
- `BrainCore.queue_proposal(p) -> {ok, status}` mirrors `propose_update` into `user://brains/<id>/pending/<pid>.proposal.json` (`phoenix.owner_proposal/1`, state `PendingApproval`). It validates ids, caps descriptions at 500 chars, refuses sensitive-looking text, dedupes, allows 10/hour and max 50 pending.
- `BrainCore.owner_proposals(id, pending_only)` and `BrainCore.sync_owner_decisions(EveCore.proposals())` mirror the owner's decision. Only `EveCore.decide()` (owner-gated) can approve.
- `BrainCore.adapter_root` (default `user://brains`) can be redirected for tests.

## Files on disk
```
res://companions/<id>/brain/            # seed (shipped, read-only)
  manifest.json
  <cell_id>.cell.json
user://brains/<id>/                     # per device
  cells/<cell_id>.cell.json             # learned/approved (override seed by id)
  pending/<cell_id>.cell.json           # proposals awaiting the player
  versions/<cell_id>.v<n>.json          # every committed version (rollback)
  memory/facts.jsonl, memory/episodes.jsonl
  audit.jsonl                           # proposed / commit / rollback / rejected
```

## Cell format (`phoenix.brain_cell/1`, schema: `data/schema/brain_cell.schema.json`)
```json
{ "schema": "phoenix.brain_cell/1", "id": "greet", "companion": "foxy_ani",
  "trigger":   {"type": "chat_keyword", "any": ["hello", "hi"]},
  "condition": {"all": [{"affinity_gte": -20}]},
  "action":    {"type": "say", "text": "Hey {player}! Rise from the flame."},
  "weight": 0.6, "version": 1, "enabled": true,
  "provenance": {"source": "seed", "author": "dev_bot", "created_at": "...", "reason": "greeting"} }
```
- **Triggers:** `chat_keyword` (any of ≤16 words), `event` (name), `need_below` (need, value), `always`.
- **Conditions:** `affinity_gte/lte`, `fact_contains`, `mood_is`, `is_lead`, `time_of_day`.
- **Actions:** `say` (≤400 chars, `{player}`/`{name}` placeholders only), `emote`, `remember`, `tool` (persona-whitelisted, still checked again by `AgentBrain.dispatch_tool`), `delegate` (lead only).

## Safe self-update loop
1. The companion experiences things, which land in `episodes.jsonl`.
2. `BrainLearner.learn()` makes proposals.
3. `BrainCore.propose()` validates them. It is **data only** (no expressions, scripts or code paths), with a rate limit of 6/hour, max 50 pending, max 200 cells, a 4 KB cell cap and a sensitive-data check.
4. **High-risk** actions (`tool`, `delegate`) always go to `pending/`. Low-risk ones (`say`/`emote`/`remember`) also go to pending by default; `auto_apply_low_risk` must be explicitly enabled.
5. The player approves or rejects. Approval re-validates and commits a new version. `rollback()` restores the previous version or removes the learned cell.
6. Weight reinforcement is the only automatic change. It is bounded and versioned, and it never adds new behavior.

## Coordination
Foxy Ani (`hierarchy.is_primary_controller`) is the bus lead. A group task becomes a plan: the lead plus any member whose abilities match the task text (everyone for follow/stay). Each step becomes a normal permission-checked tool call. Only the lead may hold `delegate` cells.

## Grok Bot portability
`BrainCore.export_portable()` produces `phoenix.brain_export/1` with cells, facts and a usage note. A standalone Grok Bot can paste cells into its instructions and facts into its memory. Cells must never be executed, and nothing in this system can alter the Grok model itself.

## Honest limits
- This is a rule-based, weighted, data-driven system. It is **not** a neural network and it does not rewrite its own code.
- The learner uses simple pattern heuristics. It will propose odd cells sometimes, which is why approval exists.
- The redaction is a basic safety net, not a privacy guarantee. Don't type secrets into chat.
- The approval UI is not built yet; approve/reject is a script API for now.
- `persona_registry.gd` is still an unregistered scaffold and isn't used by the brain.

BuildToolsAndTiers.text:
# In-world Build Tools, Roles & Tiers (design spec)

> **Status:** design spec, 2026-10-17. Most of this is **Planned**. Each section marks what is **Built** (in the code on `main` today), **Partial**, or **Planned**. Currency features are marked **LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED**.
>
> **Who builds what.** Foxy (UI lead) implements the **build engine and the build-tool HUD after v0.12 merges**. Roles and tiers are **built**: `scripts/security/tiers.gd` (`Tiers.can`, PR #26, merged as `1a07535`) is the source of truth, with the owner-only role editor in Admin › Community › Roles and the wiki page `docs/wiki/tiers.md`. The Dev Bot (this doc) owns the spec, admin, security, wiki, tickets, the ads and rental carousels, the events board, land info panels and the tier editor screen. Full split: [§9 Ownership](#9-ownership).

## 1. Goals
- Second Life / Firestorm-class build tools, rebuilt for voxels on a phone: one-handed, big targets, no tiny gizmo handles.
- Mainly for **bots and staff** (companions, employees). Other users get **tiered** access: what you can build depends on your role and on the parcel.
- Our own code first: the build engine, gizmos, grid and permission overlay are GDScript on Zylann godot_voxel. No third-party build plugins.
- Every build action is permission-checked, logged, undoable, and stoppable by the e-stop.

## 2. What exists today (grep of `main`, 2026-10-17)
| Piece | Where | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Terrain brush: Raise, Lower, Flatten, Smooth, Noise, Revert, with size 1–12 m and strength | `scripts/world/terraform.gd` (`Terraform.apply`, `brush_value`), land panel in `scripts/ui/ui_root.gd` | **Built** |
| Companion build tools: `place_voxel`, `carve_area` (sphere, r ≤ 8), `spawn_structure` (tower, hut, arch, pillar, wall, fire_altar), `build_realm` | `scripts/agent/companion_agent.gd` `tool_*`, dispatched by `AgentBrain.dispatch_tool` | **Built** |
| Tool allow-list per companion (`persona.json` tools) + e-stop (`AutonomyGuard.paused()` blocks every tool) | `scripts/autoload/agent_brain.gd` | **Built** |
| Build log: every companion build and owner terraform goes to Eve Core (`log_build`) and the revision timeline (`ViperAdminData.record_world_edit`, summaries only) | `scripts/ai/eve_core.gd`, `scripts/admin/tracker/viper_admin_data.gd` | **Built** |
| Realm presets (whole-realm generation) | `scripts/autoload/realm_builder.gd`, `data/realm_presets/` | **Built** |
| Estate: region + 64 m parcel settings (access lists, terraform rights, fly/build/damage switches, media/music URL), encrypted save | `scripts/world/estate.gd` | **Partial**: `Tiers.can(…, "build", parcel)` now reads `allow_build`, `terraform`, access lists and bans, companion tools call `Tiers.can` through `LandGate` (AUDIT-4) and `allow_damage` / `allow_fly` are read by `LandGate` (AUDIT-3; player wiring is `patches/player_fly_estate_rule.patch`); the terraform brush still doesn't call `Tiers.can`; the land panel passes `true` as "is owner" to `can_terraform` (fix proposed in `patches/land_tools_terraform_owner_check.patch`) |
| 16-material voxel palette with glitter emission | `scripts/generators/voxel_palette.gd` | **Partial**: tested, not used at runtime. The build engine's material picker should use it. |
| Procedural props + placeholder landmarks | `scripts/world/prop_kit.gd`, `landmark_builder.gd` | **Built** (placeholders) |
| Land tiers, upload fees (placeholder AEC prices) | `data/economy/land_and_fees.json` | **Data only** |
| Order book (Lindex-style), ledger | `scripts/economy/currency_exchange.gd`, `ledger.gd` | **Scaffold**, not in the UI. LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. |
| Select / move / rotate / scale, linking, properties panel, undo stack, permission overlay, blueprints, copy/paste | none | **Planned** (this doc) |
| Roles & tiers, `Tiers.can`, owner-only role editor | `scripts/security/tiers.gd`, `scripts/admin/community_screen.gd` (PR #26) | **Built** (not yet called by any build path) |

## 3. Build engine (Foxy implements, after v0.12)
Every action below calls **`Tiers.can(actor, "build", parcel)`** first (`upload` for uploads; the proposed `carve` / `paint` keys in §5 once `tiers.gd` adds them). A `false` result shows a toast ("You can't build here") and does nothing. The engine never edits voxels directly from UI code; it goes through one `BuildOp` path so permissions, undo, logging and the e-stop are always applied.

### 3.1 Operations
| Op | What it does | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Place** | Add voxels with the current brush/shape and material | Raycast from the camera (the v0.1 `player_controller.gd` raycast, now INACTIVE, is the reference) |
| **Carve** | Remove voxels with the brush/shape | Same as `carve_area`, any shape |
| **Paint** | Change material only, keep shape | Material picker = `VoxelPalette` (16 ids) + estate land textures |
| **Select** | Box or lasso a voxel region or a linked object | Selection = AABB + optional mask, shown as a platinum outline |
| **Move / Rotate / Scale** | Gizmo on the selection | Rotate snaps 15°/90°; scale is voxel-integer on blocky, free on smooth SDF |
| **Copy / Paste** | Copy the selection into a clipboard blueprint, paste with a ghost preview | Paste checks the target parcel, not the source |
| **Blueprints** | Saved, named selections (JSON: size, palette, run-length voxel data, author, version) | Bots and staff can place blueprints by name, like `spawn_structure` today |
| **Link / Unlink** | Group several selections or props into one object with a root | Like SL linksets; the root holds the properties |
| **Undo / Redo** | Per-actor stack, 50 steps | Stores before/after voxel blocks of the touched AABB only |

### 3.2 Brush & shapes
Sphere, cube, cylinder, cone, wedge, plane (wall), line (two taps), and "fill" (flood within a selection). Size uses the ring dial (1–12 m, same limits as `Terraform.MIN_SIZE`/`MAX_SIZE`), strength 0–100%. Smooth terrain uses SDF brushes (`Terraform.brush_value` falloff); blocky builds use exact voxels.

### 3.3 Snap & grid
Grid sizes 0.25 / 0.5 / 1 / 2 / 4 m, shown as a faint platinum grid on the target face only (never a full-screen grid). Snap to grid, to face, and to parcel edge. Rotation snap 15° / 90°.

### 3.4 Properties panel
For a selection or linked object: name, description, owner, creator, material, size, position (editable numbers), linked parts, permissions (copy / modify / transfer, as in SL), "for sale" (price in AEC, LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED), and the parcel it sits on. Opens as a bottom sheet.

### 3.5 Permissions overlay
A toggle that tints parcels on the ground: soft **OK** green where you may build, nothing where you may not, gold outline on your own parcels. It reads the same `Tiers.can` answer the engine uses, so the overlay can never disagree with the engine.

### 3.6 Bot & companion build API (BrainCore / AgentBrain tools)
- Keep the existing tools (`place_voxel`, `carve_area`, `spawn_structure`, `build_realm`) and add `paint_area`, `place_blueprint(name, x, y, z, rot)`, `copy_region`, `undo_last`.
- Each tool call goes `AgentBrain.dispatch_tool` → allow-list check → e-stop check → **`Tiers.can(companion_id, "build", parcel)`** → `BuildOp`. Bots that build for the owner get the **Builder/Staff** tier from the owner with **`Tiers.set_role(companion_id, "staff")`** (owner session required; each change is an audit revision `role/<id>`). Live since fix/audit-gates: `LandGate.companion_tool_error` maps `place_voxel`/`carve_area`/`spawn_structure` to `build` and `build_realm` to `land`.
- Rate limit per bot (for example 12 tool calls per turn, the current `MAX_TOOLS_PER_TURN`, plus a voxel budget per minute per parcel).
- Learned build habits stay **data-only brain cells** that need owner approval (`BrainLearner` → Proposals). A bot can never grant itself a role or a parcel right.
- Every bot build is logged (`EveCore.log_build` + a revision) and can be undone by the owner or an estate manager.

## 4. Roles (`scripts/security/tiers.gd`, built in PR #26)
`Tiers` is the source of truth; this section only summarises it. Tiers, lowest to highest: **Guest** (`guest`), **Resident** (`resident`), **Premium/Creator** (`creator`), **Builder/Staff** (`staff`, bots and employees), **Estate Manager** (`estate_manager`), **Owner** (`owner`).
- The default tier is **Guest**. A device with a saved profile is Resident.
- **Owner** also needs an unlocked owner session (`Profile.is_owner()`); a locked owner counts as Guest.
- Role changes are **owner-only** (`Tiers.set_tier`, Admin › Community › Roles). Nobody can be made Owner; `admin` and `roles` are owner-only actions.
- Roles and matrix overrides are saved to `user://social/roles.json` through `SecureFile` (encrypted once an OwnerVault exists).
- With the e-stop on (`AutonomyGuard.paused()`), bots can only `browse`.
- **Note for the build engine:** `Tiers.assigned_tier` gives companions **Resident** by default. Resident can build only where the parcel's terraform rule is `everyone`, or `group` with membership/allow-list. For bots to build on owner-only land, the owner assigns them **Builder/Staff** in the role editor (or a `bot:` id gets Staff). This is deliberate: bots never raise their own tier.

Stable API every build caller uses:
```gdscript
Tiers.can(actor, action: String, target = null) -> bool
# actor: "self", a member id, or {"id": ..., "tier": ...} (a Dictionary may only lower the tier)
# target for build/land/enter: {"region": r, "parcel": p}, "region/parcel" or "region"
```
For `build`, `land` and `enter` it combines the tier with Estate bans, access lists, group land, `allow_build` and the terraform rule (`Tiers._land_ok`).

## 5. What each tier can do
Built action keys in `Tiers.ACTIONS` that matter here, with the default matrix (each tier has everything of the tiers below it):
| Key | Lowest tier | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `enter` | Guest | plus parcel access rules |
| `build` | Resident | plus `allow_build` + terraform rule; Staff and up may build on owner-only land |
| `event_create` | Premium/Creator | hosting events (events board) |
| `classified` | Premium/Creator | classifieds tied to ad slots (SOCIAL-7) |
| `upload` | Premium/Creator | mesh/texture/sound; fees LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED |
| `marketplace` | Premium/Creator | selling; AEC pricing LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED |
| `moderate` | Builder/Staff | moderation queue |
| `land` | Estate Manager | region/estate settings and land |
| `admin`, `roles` | Owner only | admin writes, role editor |

**Proposed new keys** (to add to `tiers.gd` in its own PR, owner of `tiers.gd` decides): `carve` (terrain brush, separate from voxel `build`), `paint`, `land_rent`, `advertise` (book an ad slot; `classified` may cover it), `blueprint_place` for bots. Until then the build engine uses `build` for place/carve/paint/copy/paste/blueprints, exactly as Foxy's spec says: every action calls `Tiers.can(actor, "build", parcel)`.

A **sandbox** is a public build area (terraform rule `everyone`) that auto-cleans, like SL sandboxes; planned per region.

## 6. Land, rentals, ads, events
### 6.1 Rentals (Planned; LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED for any AEC price)
- **Parcel rental**: a parcel (64 m grid cell or a merged group of cells) for a period.
- **Region rental**: a whole region, estate manager rights delegated for the period.
- **Time-based**: hourly/daily slots for events and shops.
- Rental object: `{parcel_ids, renter, start, end, price_aec, auto_renew, voxel_budget}` stored with the estate (`user://estate.cfg` today; grid service later). When a rental ends, builds are returned to the renter's inventory as a blueprint, never deleted.
- Planned: `Tiers.can(renter, "build", parcel)` returns true only between `start` and `end` (needs rental data in `Tiers._land_ok`).

### 6.2 Advertising slots (Planned)
- **Billboards**: fixed in-world frames on parcels (the 7 landmark placeholder frames are candidates).
- **In-world carousels**: a 3D glass frame that shows one ad card at a time with the kit carousel behaviour (§7).
- Booking needs `classified` today (or a future `advertise` key); an estate manager or the owner approves each ad before it shows. No tracking, no third-party ad networks.
- Ad card: image (webp, ≤ 512 px, ETC2/ASTC on device), title ≤ 40 chars, one link target (a parcel, event or marketplace item, not a web URL by default).

### 6.3 Events board (Planned)
- A list of events (title, host, parcel, start/end in the viewer's local time, category, capacity).
- Hosts need `event_create`. Events link to their parcel ("Teleport" button) and show in the land info panel.
- Shown as a glass carousel of upcoming events on the admin Home and in the world map.

### 6.4 Land info panel (Partial)
Built today: the Region / Estate panel (texture, water, sun, access, terraform, fly/build/damage switches, media). Planned: a read-only "About Land" panel for everyone with parcel name, owner, area, voxel budget used/total, rental status and end date, for-sale price (LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED), current events, and the permission summary from `Tiers.can`.

## 7. UI (Phoenix Glass, calm premium)
Reuse the kit; do not invent new styles:
- `scenes/ui/kit/`: ring stat, radial menu, glass card, line graph, and the new **`glass_carousel.tscn`** and **`glass_menu.tscn`** (built in BUILD-1; see UI_DESIGN_LANGUAGE §12).
- `themes/phoenix_glass.tres`, `shaders/ui_glass.gdshader`, and `scripts/ui/kit/phoenix_tokens.gd` for **every** color, size and timing. Never hard-code values.

**Carousel spec** (`scenes/ui/kit/glass_carousel.tscn`): snaps one card per swipe; page dots under the card; auto-advance **only** when the list opts in (ads, event lists), never for content the user is reading; any touch pauses auto-advance.

**Motion and layout rules (from Foxy):**
- Transitions 180–240 ms, ease-out. No bounce, no spin.
- At most **one accent glow** per screen.
- The **ember** accent only on Foxy-related items.
- Tap targets **≥ 80 px**. Labels **≥ 16 sp** (Phoenix has eye strain).
- **Sizing:** Phoenix wants **Compact** as the default (smallest usable text and icons) with a **Large** toggle. The scale variables are being added to `phoenix_tokens.gd` on `feature/phone-display-media`; build-tool UI must read sizes from those tokens, never fixed numbers. The 80 px / 16 sp floors above apply to the Large setting and to anything Phoenix taps often; Compact must still meet platform minimums (48 dp tap targets).
- Premium and restrained: generous spacing, few glass layers (≤ 3), no flashing, no confetti, no campy effects.

**Build HUD (Foxy's, spec only):** bottom-third layout; the operation is a radial menu (Place, Carve, Paint, Select, Move, Copy/Paste, Undo), the brush size is a ring dial, materials are a carousel of palette swatches, the gizmo has three big drag rings (not thin arrows), and the properties panel is a bottom sheet. The permissions overlay toggle sits next to the brush dial.

## 8. Real-world ties (concepts)

DataMysqlAndBackup.text:
# Data Storage, MySQL Sync & Backup

> **Planned module, not implemented. No live servers or services exist.** Phase: 4 (local) / 9 (server sync).

## On device (default)
- World chunks are stored in `VoxelStreamSQLite` (`user://worlds/<realm>.sqlite`).
- Game data (inventory, needs, relationships, settings) goes in a separate SQLite DB `user://phoenix.db`, through a godot-sqlite GDExtension that has to be vetted for Android arm64.
- Brains are plain files under `user://brains/<id>/` (see BRAIN_FILES.md).
- Schema migrations use a `schema_version` table and ordered migration scripts.

## Optional MySQL server sync (future, opt-in)
- The game **never talks to MySQL directly**. A small HTTPS API (e.g. a REST service in front of MySQL/MariaDB) gives auth, rate limits, and keeps DB credentials off the phone.
- Sync model: each record carries `uuid`, `updated_at` and `device_id`, using last-write-wins plus a conflict log. World chunks sync as compressed blobs, edited chunks only.
- Off by default, enabled in Settings with an account. Privacy policy required.

## Backup / restore
- **Local export:** zip `phoenix.db` + world DBs + brains → `Phoenix_backup_<date>.zip` via the Android share sheet or Storage Access Framework.
- **Restore:** pick the zip, validate the manifest + schema version, then swap atomically (keep the previous copy until it succeeds).
- Android Auto Backup rules exclude large world files by default (a setting can include them).
- Optional encrypted backups (passphrase → key) for brains.

DnaGenetics.text:
# DNA / Genetics

> **Future module, not implemented.** Phase: Phase 7. Design notes only.

Star Citizen-style DNA blending for faces and bodies, adapted to voxel/mesh characters.
- **Genome** is a JSON vector of morph weights (face shape, eyes, nose, jaw, body height and build) plus palette genes (hair, eye and skin colors) and trait genes (emissive accents, fire essence).
- **Blending:** choose 2–3 "parents" (e.g. Aaliyah + Foxy Ani + Circuit Nova accents, matching the CHARACTER_BLUEPRINT inheritance rules). The child is a weighted lerp plus small mutation noise.
- **Rendering:** for mesh bodies, genes drive blend shapes on a base mesh. For voxel bodies, genes pick voxel part variants and palettes.
- Stored as `genome` in persona.json (future schema v3) so the standalone bot's avatar art can match.
- Original characters only; no scanning of real people's likenesses.

# Economy & Banking — PLAN (VIRTUAL CURRENCY ONLY)
> ⚠️ **The currency is virtual only.** It has no cash value and can't be bought, sold, or redeemed for real money. **Any real-money feature (purchases, cash-out, exchange to fiat, trading between players for money) is blocked until Anterrania Law Bot does a legal review and Anterranian explicitly approves.** Money-transmission, gambling, consumer-protection, and app-store rules may apply.

- **Currency:** "Phoenix Embers" (working name), Linden-dollar-style soft currency earned through quests, trade skills, and building. A second premium-style currency is NOT planned.
- **Exchange (Lindex-like):** an in-game order book between Embers and in-game commodities or a second in-game token. Limit/market orders, a spread, and fees that are destroyed (a sink). `scripts/economy/currency_exchange.gd` is a stub.
- **Ledger/banking:** double-entry, append-only ledger (`scripts/economy/ledger.gd`). Every transfer is a debit plus a credit with matching amounts. Balances are derived from entries. Amounts are integers (no floats). Optional bank accounts for realms/guilds, plus interest as a game mechanic.
- **Sinks/faucets:** track both. Ledger Vale (economy-advisor persona) explains them in-game.
- Persistence: local first. Later MySQL tables `ledger_entries`, `accounts`, `orders` (DATA_MYSQL_AND_BACKUP.md).

GrindingProgression.text:
# Grinding & Progression — PLAN
- **Trade skills (New World-style):** gathering (mining, logging, harvesting, skinning, fishing), refining (smelting, weaving, tanning), and crafting (weaponsmith, engineering, cooking, arcana). Each skill goes to level 200. Refined goods feed the economy (ECONOMY_BANKING.md).
- **Skill-by-use (Skyrim-style):** doing an action earns XP in that skill (`scripts/progression/skill_by_use.gd`). XP per level goes up on a curve. Character level comes from total skill-ups. Companions learn skills too, and DNA traits change their learning rate.
- **Pets / heroes / gems (League of Angels-style):** collectible companion pets and hero forms with star tiers, gem sockets (fire/circuit/grace), and awakening. **No paid gacha.** Everything is earned in-game unless the Law Bot reviews a monetization plan.
- Anti-grind guardrails: daily diminishing returns, catch-up XP, offline progress capped at 8h.
